dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شِيَعاً): In al-Qāmūs, al-Tāj and other lexicons: "A man's shīʿa are his followers and supporters; the plural is shiyaʿ and ashyāʿ. Al-shīʿa is a faction, and it applies to one, two and many, masculine and feminine. This name has come to be applied predominantly to everyone who takes ʿAlī and the people of his house as patrons, until it became a name specific to them; the singular is shīʿī." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Shiyaʿan: factions who follow him in whatever he wants and obey him, none of them able to turn his neck away. Al-Aʿshā said:
وبلدة يرهب الجواب دلجتها ... حتى تراه عليها يبتغي الشيعا
(Many a land whose night journey the seasoned traveller dreads, so that you see him in it seeking companions.)
Or: some of them follow others in obeying him; or: classes [of people] in his service, employing one class in building, one class in tilling and one class in digging, and whoever he did not employ he imposed tribute upon; or: divergent factions among whom he stirred up enmity." The meaning of the verse al-Zamakhsharī cited from al-Aʿshā: Many a desert the jawwāb — that is, the much-travelled one, from jubtu al-arḍa, "I crossed the land by travelling" — fears; and al-dulja is from dalaja, adlaja and iddalaja, to travel by night, al-dulja being an hour of the night. That is: the one accustomed to travel fears travelling through it by night, so that he seeks groups who will help him travel through it. After the verse come his words:
كلفت مجهولها نفسي وشايعني ... همّي عليها إذا ما آلها لمعا
(I burdened myself with its unknown tracts, and my resolve accompanied me over it when its mirage gleamed.)
بذات لوث عفرناة إذا عثرت ... فالتعس أولى لها من أن يقال لعا
(On a strong, stout she-camel; if she stumbles, "May she fall!" suits her better than "Rise up!")
He says: I burdened myself with travelling its unknown parts, and my resolve returned to me for travelling through it at the time its āl gleamed — the āl being the mirage seen in intense heat as though it were water — even though travelling in the midday heat is harder than travelling by night. Then he said: with a she-camel possessed of strength; lawth is also used for weakness, so it is one of the aḍdād (words with opposite meanings). ʿAfarnāh: thick-set. To one who stumbles it is said "laʿan laka," a prayer for him to recover, and "taʿsan lahu," a prayer against him that he fall. He means that she does not stumble, and were she to stumble, the prayer against her would be more fitting for her than the prayer for her.
(وَيَسْتَحْيِي نِساءَهُمْ): he kept them alive, because one of the soothsayers had told him that a child would be born among the Children of Israel who would be the cause of the end of his kingdom.
(هامانَ): the vizier of Pharaoh mentioned here. [There is also] Haman the enemy of the Jews, the vizier of Ahasuerus the Persian, mentioned in the Book of Esther among the books of the Old Testament.

* I'rab:
(طسم تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ): What is to be said about it has already preceded. (تلك) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (آيات الكتاب المبين) its khabar (predicate). (نَتْلُوا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ نَبَإِ مُوسى وَفِرْعَوْنَ بِالْحَقِّ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): (نتلو) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "naḥnu". (عليك) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (نتلو). (من نبأ) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "something of the story of Moses and Pharaoh"; in it the qualified noun is omitted and the adjective put in its place. (بالحق) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (نتلو), i.e. "while We are clothed in truth and veracity", or from the object, i.e. "while it is clothed in truth and veracity". (لقوم) is attached to (نتلو), and it stands as its reason, i.e. "for the sake of a people". The clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم). (إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَها شِيَعاً): a resumptive statement brought to set out the story of Pharaoh, or an explicative clause for the tidings of Moses; both of them have no grammatical position. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (علا) is its khabar; the agent of (علا) is a pronoun latent by option, its implied form being "huwa", i.e. Pharaoh. (في الأرض) is attached to (علا). (جعل أهلها): a verb, a latent agent and the first object; (شيعا) is the second object. (يَسْتَضْعِفُ طائِفَةً مِنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْناءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيِي نِساءَهُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ مِنَ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the clause (يستضعف) is a ḥāl from the agent of (جعل), or an adjective of (شيعا), and you may make it a resumptive statement. The agent of (يستضعف) is "huwa", and (طائفة) is the direct object; (منهم) is an adjective of (طائفة). (يذبح) is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from (يستضعف), because the oppression includes both the slaughtering and the sparing. (أبناءهم) is the object of (يذبح), and (يستحيي نساءهم) is conjoined to (يذبح أبناءهم). The clause (إنه) is a reason for these acts: (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كان) is its khabar; the noun of (كان) is latent, its implied form being "huwa", and (من المفسدين) is the khabar of (كان). Pharaoh slaughtered their sons and left the women only because the astrologers of that age told him that his kingdom would go at the hand of a child from the Children of Israel. Al-Zajjāj said: "Astonishing is Pharaoh's folly! For if the soothsayer who told him that was truthful in his view, then killing would be of no use, and if he was lying, then there was no point in killing."
(وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial. If you make it conjunctive, you conjoin the statement to His words (إن فرعون علا في الأرض), because it is its counterpart in serving as an explanation of the tidings of Moses and Pharaoh, and the imperfect form is for narrating a past state. If you make it circumstantial, the clause is a ḥāl from (يستضعف), i.e. "Pharaoh oppresses them while We wish to bestow favour upon them". (أن) and what falls within its scope is the object of (نريد). (على الذين) is attached to (نمن), and the clause (استضعفوا) is the ṣila (relative clause). (في الأرض) is attached to (استضعفوا), or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while they are on the earth", and perhaps this is preferable. (وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ الْوارِثِينَ): (نجعلهم) is conjoined to (نمنّ); the hāʾ is the first object and (أئمة) the second object. (نجعلهم الوارثين) is conjoined to (نجعلهم أئمة). (وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ وَجُنُودَهُما مِنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَحْذَرُونَ): (نمكن) is conjoined to (نجعل), its agent latent, its implied form being "naḥnu"; (لهم) is attached to (نمكن), and (في الأرض) is a ḥāl. (نري) is also conjoined; (فرعون) is the direct object, (هامان) is conjoined to (فرعون), and (جنودهما) is conjoined to (فرعون وهامان). (منهم) is attached to (نري), i.e. "and We show Pharaoh, Haman and their hosts, from the Children of Israel, what they used to beware of", i.e. what they feared from them — and it did happen at the hand of a child from among them. (ما) is the second object of (نري); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يحذرون) is the khabar of (كانوا).

dervis-irab:47-50.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لولا) is the particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); (أن) and what falls within its scope is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, as the well-known rule has it, i.e. "and were it not for the calamity befalling them"; its answer is omitted, its implied form being "We would not have sent a messenger". (مصيبة) is the fāʿil (agent); (بما) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تصيبهم); and the clause (قدمت) is the ṣila (relative clause). (فَيَقُولُوا رَبَّنا لَوْلا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آياتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (يقولوا) is conjoined to (أن تصيبهم); (ربنا) is a muḍāf vocative (munādā); (لولا) is the particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), meaning "why not"; (أرسلت) is a verb and its agent; (إلينا) are attached to (أرسلت); (رسولا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In (فنتبع) the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation, and (نتبع) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation; the agent of (نتبع) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we"; (آياتك) is the direct object; (نكون) is conjoined to (نتبع); the noun of (نكون) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and (من المؤمنين) is its khabar.
This verse has occupied the commentators and the grammarians. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you say: How does this meaning hold good, when the punishment has been made the cause of sending, not the saying, since the particle of non-occurrence has been put on it and not on the saying? I say: The saying is what is intended to be the cause of sending the messengers; but since the punishment was the cause of the saying, and the saying exists through its existence, the punishment was made as though it were the cause of the sending by means of the saying, so لولا was put on it, and the saying was brought conjoined to it with the fāʾ that gives the sense of causation. Its meaning comes down to your saying: 'Were it not for this saying of theirs when a calamity befalls them, We would not have sent.' But this way was chosen for a subtle point, namely that if they were not, for example, punished for their unbelief, having witnessed that by which they were driven to certain knowledge, they would not say: «لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا»; rather, the cause of this saying of theirs is the punishment and nothing else, not regret at the faith in their Creator that they have missed. In this there is a strong testimony, which is not hidden, to how firmly their unbelief is rooted and established in them."
The secret of making the cause of the cause a cause, and conjoining the original cause to it, is twofold. First, that greater concern requires putting first, and this is the secret that Sībawayh pointed out. Second, that in this arrangement there is a reminder of the causality of each of the two: the first because it is joined to the particle of causation, namely أن, and the second because it is joined to the fāʾ of causation. Some grammarians used to raise a difficulty with this verse, saying: «لولا», according to the specialists, indicates the non-occurrence of its answer because of the occurrence [Translator's note: the printed text has «لوجو», evidently for «لوجود»] of what follows it. In that case what comes after it in the verse would be existent, namely the punishment of these people on the supposition that messengers were not sent, and its omitted answer would not occur, namely not sending, because it is a fortiori impossible. And when not-sending does not occur, sending necessarily occurs. So what comes after it becomes problematic, since there is no wrongdoing before the sending of messengers, and so punishment on the supposition that none were sent is inconceivable; for it occurs as recompense for violating the rulings of the Law, and if there is no Law there is no violation and no punishment. And the answer becomes problematic for the grammarians, because it is required not to occur, namely the non-sending of messengers, yet what comes after it requires its occurrence. The precise statement of the meaning of لولا is that it indicates that what follows it is a preventer of its answer, the reverse of «لو», whose meaning is that its answer is necessitated by what follows it. Then the preventer may be existent, or it may be supposed, and the verse is of the kind in which the existence of the preventer is supposed. Likewise the necessity in «لو»: one thing may be necessitated by two things, so its negation does not follow from the negation of one of the two things that necessitate it. On this precise statement the difficulty disappears.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِنا قالُوا لَوْلا أُوتِيَ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ مُوسى): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal ("when") or a linking particle; (جاءهم الحق) is a past verb, a direct object put first and an agent put after; (من عندنا) are attached to (جاءهم); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (لما); (لولا) is a particle of urging, i.e. "why not"; (أوتي) is a past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "he", i.e. Muḥammad ﷺ; (مثل) is a second direct object; (ما) is a relative noun, the muḍāf ilayhi of (مثل); the clause (أوتي) is the ṣila; and (موسى) is the deputy agent. (أَوَلَمْ يَكْفُرُوا بِما أُوتِيَ مُوسى مِنْ قَبْلُ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation; the wāw is conjoined to something implied that the context calls for; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; (يكفروا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (بما) are attached to (يكفروا); the clause (أوتي موسى) is the ṣila; (من قبل) are attached to (أولم يكفروا) or to (أوتي). The meaning then is that the people of Mecca who said this, just as they disbelieved in Muḥammad and in the Qurʾān, had disbelieved in Moses and in the Torah.
(قالُوا سِحْرانِ تَظاهَرا وَقالُوا إِنَّا بِكُلٍّ كافِرُونَ): the clause (قالوا) is explicative; (سحران) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are two sorcerers" [Translator's note: the text glosses with «ساحران» though the reading cited is «سحران»]; the clause (تظاهرا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (سحران), i.e. they supported one another, each confirming the other; (قالوا) is conjoined to (قالوا); (إنا) is inna and its noun; (بكل) are attached to (كافرون); (كافرون) is the khabar of (إنا); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِكِتابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدى مِنْهُما أَتَّبِعْهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (أتوا) is an imperative verb; (بكتاب) are attached to (فأتوا); (من عند الله) are attached to an omitted adjective; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أهدى) the khabar; (منهما) are attached to (أهدى); and the clause is a second adjective of (كتاب). (أتبعه) is an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the answer of the imperative; the agent is latent, its implied form being "I", and the hāʾ is the direct object. (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a past incomplete verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and (صادقين) its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then bring it". The imperative here is for showing inability, mixed with rebuke and reproach. (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكَ فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّما يَتَّبِعُونَ أَهْواءَهُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يستجيبوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم), and the wāw is the agent; (لك) are attached to (يستجيبوا); the fāʾ links the apodosis; (اعلم) is an imperative verb; (أنما) is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) giving the sense of restriction (ḥaṣr); (يتبعون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) with its agent; (أهواءهم) is the object; and (إنما) [Translator's note: so in the text, for «أنما»] with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (اعلم).
(وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنِ اتَّبَعَ هَواهُ بِغَيْرِ هُدىً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation and disapproval, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (أضل) is its khabar; (ممن) are attached to (أضل); the clause (اتبع هواه) is the ṣila of (من); (بغير هدى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من الله) is an adjective of (هدى); the clause (إن الله) gives the reason for what precedes; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يهدي القوم الظالمين) is its khabar.

* Benefits:
Because of the closeness of the constructions in the preceding verse, namely His saying, Exalted is He, «ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين», and the loftiness of its inimitability, we cite, in addition to what we presented in the i'rab, what al-Shihāb al-Khafājī said in his delightful gloss (ḥāshiya) on al-Bayḍāwī, for it clarifies what we have explained. He said, in summary: The verse requires the existence of their being afflicted and the existence of their said saying; but in fact they were not afflicted and did not say the said saying. So this arrangement becomes problematic, in that لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence, and the meaning would become "We sent you to them because of the calamity befalling them and the existence of their said saying", which is not correct. Some went to pains to answer that there is an omission of the muḍāf in the speech, the implied form being "and were it not for the dislike that a calamity should befall them…", so what is established as existent is only the dislike of their calamity on which their said saying follows; the meaning is then "We sent you to them for the sake of the dislike that they be afflicted and then say what was mentioned". It has also been said that the precise view is that لولا only indicates that what follows it is a preventer of its answer, and the preventer may be existent or may be supposed, and what is here is of the second kind, so there is no difficulty in it, even if the muḍāf is not supplied. End of quotation.

dervis-irab:7-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلا تَخافِي وَلا تَحْزَنِي): Fear is distress that afflicts a person because of a disliked matter that is expected; grief is distress that afflicts him because of a disliked matter that has already happened. The establishment of this, and the objection raised against this conjunction, will come in the section on rhetoric.
(قُصِّيهِ): follow his trace and track news of him; its verb pattern is that of naṣara. More explanation of this root will follow.
(جُنُبٍ), with two ḍammas: a distant place. One says baṣurtu bihi ʿan junubin and ʿan janābatin, meaning "from afar".

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى أُمِّ مُوسى أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause (أوحينا) is conjoined to His words (إن فرعون علا في الأرض); both clauses fall under the ruling of being an explanation of the tidings. (أوحينا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلى أم موسى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أوحينا). (أن) is explicative, because inspiring carries the meaning of saying without its letters; it may also be maṣdariyya in its usual sense, in which case, together with what it governs, it is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (أوحينا). (أرضعيه) is an imperative verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَإِذا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (خفت) is a verb and its agent; (عليه) is attached to (خفت). (فألقيه): the fāʾ is the connective [of the apodosis]; (ألقيه) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the yāʾ being the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. (في اليم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ألقيه); by al-yamm He meant the Nile. (وَلا تَخافِي وَلا تَحْزَنِي إِنَّا رَادُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجاعِلُوهُ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive, (لا) is prohibitive, and (تخافي) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); (لا تحزني) is conjoined to (لا تخافي). The clause (إنا رادوه) is a reason for the command and the prohibition: (إن) and its noun, and (رادوه) is its khabar (predicate); (إليك) is attached to (رادوه). (جاعلوه) is conjoined to (رادوه); the active participle has been put in genitive construct with its first object, and (من المرسلين) is in the position of the accusative as its second object. (فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted for concision, its implied form being: "So she suckled him and cast him into the river Nile in a chest she had prepared for him, and the Nile carried him to opposite Pharaoh's palace overlooking it, and Pharaoh's household picked him up"; they also call it the faṣīḥa [fāʾ]. It is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (ليكون): the lām is said to be of reason, and said to be of consequence; the details of this and a study of this lām will come in the section on benefits. (يكون) is in any case an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an optionally concealed (أن) after the lām; the noun of (يكون) is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; (عدوا) is the khabar of (يكون), and (حزنا) is conjoined to (عدوا).
(إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ وَجُنُودَهُما كانُوا خاطِئِينَ): a statement with no grammatical position, because it is a reason for the preceding matters. It is also said to be a parenthetical statement between the conjoined-to, namely (فالتقطه آل فرعون), and the conjoined, namely (وقالت امرأة فرعون). (إن) and its noun; (هامان وجنودهما) are conjoined to (فرعون); the clause (كانوا) is the khabar of (إن); (كان) and its noun, and (خاطئين) its khabar. (وَقالَتِ امْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ: قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِي وَلَكَ): the wāw is conjunctive, and (قالت) is conjoined to (فالتقطه آل فرعون). (امرأة فرعون) is the agent of (قالت); she is Āsiya bint Muzāḥim, and mention of her will come in the story of Moses and Pharaoh. (قرة عين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is a delight of the eye". (لي ولك) are two adjectives of (قرة). Some of the parsers have blundered astonishingly in parsing this verse; we will touch on it in the section on benefits. (لا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسى أَنْ يَنْفَعَنا أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُ وَلَداً وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): (لا) is prohibitive and (تقتلوه) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لا); the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. (عسى) is a past verb among the verbs of hope, and it operates as (كان) does; its noun is latent, its implied form being "huwa", and (أن ينفعنا) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the khabar of (عسى). (أو نتخذه) is conjoined to (ينفعنا); the hāʾ is the first object and (ولدا) the second object. (وهم): the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يشعرون) the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the household of Pharaoh. It is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, and it is unlikely to be from the speech of Āsiya. (وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤادُ أُمِّ مُوسى فارِغاً): the wāw is resumptive; (أصبح) is a defective past verb, (فؤاد أم موسى) its noun and (فارغا) its khabar. The explanation of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric. (إِنْ كادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ لَوْلا أَنْ رَبَطْنا عَلى قَلْبِها لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): (إن) is lightened from the heavy [inna]; (كادت) is a past verb among the verbs of proximity, its noun latent, its implied form being "hiya"; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and the clause (تبدي) is the khabar of (كادت); (به) is attached to (تبدي). If you make (إن) operative, its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (كادت) is its khabar; but it is preferable to leave it inoperative. The meaning of (لتبدي به) is: she would make manifest speech about him; the pronoun refers to Moses. It is also said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) and the hāʾ is in the position of the accusative as the direct object, but the first is more exact. (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence; (أن) is maṣdariyya, and together with what it governs it is a maṣdar in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "were it not that Our strengthening of her heart was present". (على قلبها) is attached to (ربطنا). The apodosis (jawāb) of (لولا) is omitted, i.e. "she would have disclosed him". (لتكون): the lām is of reason, and (تكون) is a defective imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to (ربطنا), and (من المؤمنين) is the khabar of (تكون).
(وَقالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (قالت) is a past verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "hiya", i.e. the mother of Moses; (لأخته) is attached to (قالت). (قصيه) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the yāʾ being the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. (فبصرت): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so she went looking for him and following his traces". (به) is attached to (بصرت), and (عن جنب) is in the place of a ḥāl from the agent of (بصرت), i.e. "she watched him in concealment, being at a distance", or from the genitive noun in (به), i.e. "[him being] far away". The wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يشعرون) the khabar.
(وَحَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِ الْمَراضِعَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَقالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ ناصِحُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to begin setting out the cause of his return to his mother. (حرمنا) is a verb and its agent; (عليه) is attached to (حرمنا); (المراضع) is the direct object, and (من قبل) is a ḥāl. — (المراضع) is the plural of murḍiʿ, a woman who practises suckling but has not [yet] undertaken it, or the plural of marḍaʿ, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ḍād, a noun of the place of suckling, meaning the breast. — (فقالت): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, i.e. "when his sister saw that, she said". (هل) is an interrogative particle; (أدلكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "anā", and the kāf is the direct object. (على أهل بيت) is attached to (أدلكم); the clause (يكفلونه) is an adjective of (أهل بيت); (لكم) is attached to (يكفلونه). The wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is the mubtadaʾ; (له) is attached to (ناصحون), and (ناصحون) is the khabar.
(فَرَدَدْناهُ إِلى أُمِّهِ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُها وَلا تَحْزَنَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (رددناه) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (إلى أمه) is attached to (رددناه). (كي) is a particle of reason and of the accusative; (تقر) is an imperfect verb accusative by (كي), and (لا تحزن) is conjoined to (تقر). The tear of joy is cool, and the eye of the anxious is hot and burning. (وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive and the lām of reason; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām. (أن) and what follows it take the place of the two objects of (تعلم): (أن) and its noun, and (حق) its khabar. The wāw is circumstantial; (لكن أكثرهم): (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The meaning of fear and grief:
Someone may ask: what is the difference between fear and grief such that one is conjoined to the other in His words «ولا تخافي ولا تحزني»? And furthermore, is it not a contradiction to affirm fear in His words «فإذا خفت عليه» and then negate it with His words «ولا تخافي»? The answer to the alleged contradiction is that the first, affirmed fear is [fear of] his drowning in the Nile, and the second is fear of the slaughter; so the imagined contradiction is removed. As for the first objection, it is removed by [noting] that this belongs to iṭnāb (amplification) — indeed it is a rare and one of the most beautiful of its kinds: namely, that a thing is mentioned and overlapping meanings are brought for it, except that each meaning is distinguished by a feature the other does not have. We said in the section on vocabulary that fear is distress afflicting a person because of a matter whose occurrence is expected in the future, whereas grief is distress afflicting him because of a matter that has actually occurred and passed; so she was forbidden both of them together. Of this kind are the words of Abū Tammām, who excelled in it:
قطعت إليّ الزابيين هباته ... والتاث مأمول السحاب المسبل
(His gifts crossed the two Zābs to reach me, while the hoped-for, pouring cloud was sluggish.)
من منة مشهورة وصنيعة ... بكر وإحسان أغر محجل
(Of a renowned favour, a virgin benefaction, and a kindness bright-blazed and white-footed.)
His words "a renowned favour, a virgin benefaction, and a kindness bright-blazed and white-footed" have overlapping meanings, since favour, benefaction and kindness are close to one another. That is not repetition, as might be imagined, because had he confined himself to saying "favour, benefaction and kindness" it could have been repetition; but he described each of these three with a quality that took it out of the ruling of repetition. He said "a renowned favour", describing it as renowned because of its great importance; "a virgin benefaction", describing it as virgin, i.e. its like had never been done before; and "a kindness bright-blazed and white-footed", describing it with the blaze and the white feet, i.e. it possesses many fine qualities. Since he described these overlapping meanings, which indicate a single thing, with distinct descriptions, it became iṭnāb and was not repetition.
This verse — «وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين» — contains two commands, namely «أرضعيه» and «فألقيه»; two prohibitions, namely «لا تخافي» and «لا تحزني»; two statements, namely «إنا رادوه إليك» and «وجاعلوه من المرسلين»; and, contained within the two statements, two glad tidings, namely his return to her and his being made one of the messengers.

2- Kināya (metonymy):
This is in His words «وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا», for that is a kināya for loss of reason and the mind's being unhinged. The meaning is that when she heard he had fallen into Pharaoh's hands, her senses were lost and her reason flew away because of the excessive anguish and bewilderment that overcame her. Like it are the words of the Exalted «وأفئدتهم هواء», i.e. hollow, with no minds in them; and of it is the verse of Ḥassān:
ألا أبلغ أبا سفيان عني ... فأنت مجوّف نخب هواء
(Convey from me to Abū Sufyān: you are hollow, cowardly, empty.)
This verse is from a long ode by Ḥassān ibn Thābit in which he satirises Abū Sufyān before his Islam, and after it [comes]:
بأن سيوفنا تركت عبيدا ... وعبد الدار سادتها الإماء
(That our swords have left [the tribes of] ʿUbayd and ʿAbd al-Dār with slave-women as their masters.)
هجوت محمدا فأجبت عنه ... وعند الله في ذاك الجزاء
(You satirised Muḥammad and I answered on his behalf, and with Allah is the reward for that.)
أتهجوه ولست له بكفء ... فشرّ كما لخير كما الفداء أمن يهجو رسول الله منكم ... ويمدحه وينصره
سواء فإن أبي ووالده وعرضي ... لعرض محمد منكم وقاء
(Do you satirise him when you are not his equal? May the worse of you two be ransom for the better of you two. Is the one of you who satirises the Messenger of Allah and the one who praises and supports him equal? For my father, his father and my honour are a shield for the honour of Muḥammad against you.)
«[Translator's note: the line division of the last two verses is garbled in the source; they are reproduced exactly as printed.]»
(ألا) is a particle of alerting and opening; the one commanded to convey is unspecified. Then he turned [to address him directly] (iltifāt) to provoke Abū Sufyān's rage; the context required him to say "fa-innahu", i.e. Abū Sufyān, but addressing him and confronting him face to face with censure is more painful to the soul and more scathing in satire. Mujawwaf, nakhib and hawāʾ [mean] empty-bellied, or with a heart void of reason and courage. Attributing the leaving to the swords is a majāz ʿaqlī (rational metaphor), because they are the instrument of the act. ʿUbayd, in the diminutive, is a tribe, and likewise ʿAbd al-Dār. (سادتها) is a mubtadaʾ and (الإماء) its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the second object of (تركت), i.e. "they made ʿUbayd have no masters but women, and made ʿAbd al-Dār likewise". In (أتهجوه) the interrogative is one of denial and rebuke, and the wāw after it is circumstantial, i.e. that is not fitting for you. Sharr and khayr are two elatives (ism tafḍīl) distinguished by dropping their hamza for lightness because of their frequent use; but what is meant by them here is the base quality, not the excess in it. The worse one is Abū Sufyān. The clause (فشر كما لخير كما الفداء) is a supplication: he prayed against him that he be a ransom for the Messenger of Allah, and he set it out in the form of ambiguity for the sake of fairness in speech; that is why, when those present heard it, they said: "This is the fairest verse the Arabs have ever said." (أمن يهجو) is an interrogative of denial, i.e. the one of you who satirises him and the one of us who praises and supports him are not equal. It is possible that the hamza is for alerting or for the vocative, the one addressed being omitted, i.e. "O people of Abū Sufyān, the one of you who satirises the Messenger of Allah and the one of you who praises and supports him are equal in not being worth heeding." Wiqāʾ is that by which a disliked thing is guarded against, on the pattern of ḥizām and ribāṭ, so it is either in the sense of a passive participle or a noun of instrument.

* Benefits:
1- The story of Moses and Pharaoh:
We summarise here the story of Moses and Pharaoh as it has been narrated, because of its charm and as has been our practice in this book. Mūsā means "water and trees", because mū in Coptic is water and shā is trees; it was Arabised, and he was named Mūsā because they found him between the two. He is Moses son of ʿImrān, tracing his lineage to Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham. The Children of Israel had remained under the hands of the Pharaohs since the time of Joseph, until there came the Pharaoh to whom Moses was sent. There was no Pharaoh among them more tyrannical or longer-lived than he, and he was extremely harsh; his name was al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab. He had taken the Children of Israel as servants: one class of them building, one class tilling, and whoever had no work he levied tribute upon. He saw in a dream that a fire came from Jerusalem (al-Maqdis) and burned the Copts. He asked about his dream and was told: "From this land — i.e. the one the Children of Israel came from — a man will come forth at whose hands will be the ruin of Egypt." So he ordered every newborn killed, until he almost annihilated them. It was said to him: "They are only your servants, and if you annihilate them the line will be cut off." So he ordered the boys killed one year and spared one year. Aaron was born in the year in which they were spared, and Moses was born in the year in which they were killed. When she gave birth to him she grieved, and Allah inspired her: «أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم». So she made a chest, put him in it and cast it into the yamm, which is the Nile, and said to his sister: «قصيه». The water carried him until it brought him in among dense trees beneath Pharaoh's palace. Pharaoh's maidservants came out to bathe and found the chest, and they brought it in to Āsiya, Pharaoh's wife. When she saw him she loved him and told Pharaoh about him. He wanted to slaughter him, fearing that he might be the newborn he had been warned about, but Āsiya kept at him until he left him to her. That is His words «فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا». The rest of the story will follow.
2- The lām of consequence (al-ʿāqiba) or of becoming (al-ṣayrūra):
The lām in «ليكون» is of consequence. What it governs has been presented in the guise of a reason for their picking him up, likening it — in its following from that — to the purpose that motivates it. It is called the lām of becoming and the lām of outcome. The Basrans denied the lām of consequence. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The precise view is that it is the lām of reason, and that the reasoning in it comes by way of majāz (figurative usage), not literally; for their motive for picking him up was not that he should be an enemy and a grief to them, but love and adoption. However, since that was the result and fruit of their picking him up, it was likened to the motive for whose sake the doer does the act — like honouring, which is the result of coming, and being disciplined, which is the fruit of beating, in your saying 'I beat him so that he would be disciplined.' Its precise statement is that the ruling of this lām is the ruling of 'lion', in that it has been borrowed for what resembles reason, just as 'lion' is borrowed for one who resembles a lion."

3- Parsings of «قرة أعين»:
«[Translator's note: the verse reads (قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ); the heading writes «قرة أعين», as printed in the source.]»
In this book we have avoided citing weaker parsings, let alone incoherent ones, because we have preferred to choose the best and most exemplary of the possible analyses. However, we do not see fit to ignore some of the incoherent parsings that some parsers have adopted. We said that (قرة أعين) is the khabar of a concealed mubtadaʾ, and (لي ولك) are two adjectives. Some permitted an analysis that cannot be admitted at all, namely that (قرة أعين) is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the clause (لا تقتلوه), because in it a performative (inshāʾ) is used as the predicate of a declarative. This is a small matter compared to the mismatch of the pronoun, for he would have had to say "lā taqtulūhā" [feminine]. They argued that since what is meant is masculine, that is permissible — and how unneeded [the Qurʾān] is of such far-fetched contrivance, which does not befit the Qurʾān! Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted, with his chain to Ibn ʿAbbās, that he paused at «لا», i.e. "He is a delight of the eye for me only, and for you, no", i.e. he is not a delight of the eye; then he would begin with His words "taqtulūhu". This is laughable and cannot be attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, nor to Ibn al-Anbārī himself. How could (تقتلوه) remain without the nūn of the nominative, with nothing requiring its omission? That is why al-Farrāʾ said:
It is a solecism (laḥn).

dervis-irab:51-56.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ وَصَّلْنا لَهُمُ الْقَوْلَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and you may make it a conjunction so that the speech runs on consistently; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (وصّلنا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (لهم) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to (وصلنا); (القول) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. We made part of it follow part in the sending down, so that the reminding would be continuous. (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (يتذكرون) is the khabar (predicate) of (لعلّ), i.e. We made it varied, containing promise and threat, counsels, admonitions and stories, so that they might take admonition from it. (الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ هُمْ بِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ): (الذين) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila (relative clause); (آتيناهم) is a verb, its agent and a first direct object; (الكتاب) is a second direct object; (من قبله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنون); the clause (يؤمنون) is the khabar of «هم», and the clause (هم به يؤمنون) is the khabar of (الذين). They are the People of the Book who believed; they numbered forty men, and it is said eighty. (وَإِذا يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ قالُوا آمَنَّا بِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause (يتلى) is in the position of genitive through the adverb being put in construct (iḍāfa) with it; (يتلى) is a passive imperfect verb; (عليهم) are attached to (يتلى); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it", referring to the Qurʾān; the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; the clause (آمنا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and (به) are attached to (آمنا). (إِنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّنا إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مُسْلِمِينَ): resumptive speech, set out to state and give the reason for what called for their faith in it. (إن) and its noun; (الحق) is the khabar of (إن); (من ربنا) is a ḥāl. (إنا كنا…) is also resumptive speech, set out to show that their faith was not an innovation or something newly arisen but a matter of long standing. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كنا) is its khabar; (من قبله) is a ḥāl; and (مسلمين) is the khabar of (كنا), because islām is the description of every believer who affirms the revelation.
(أُولئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ بِما صَبَرُوا): (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يؤتون) the khabar; (يؤتون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the deputy agent; (أجرهم) is a second direct object; (مرتين) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as an adverb; (بما صبروا) are attached to (يؤتون); the bāʾ is a preposition of causation and (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their patience". (وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ): (يدرءون) is conjoined to (يؤتون), i.e. "they repel", and the wāw is the agent; (بالحسنة) are attached to (يدرءون); (السيئة) is the direct object; (مما) are attached to (ينفقون); the clause (رزقناهم) is the ṣila; and (ينفقون) is conjoined to (يدرءون). (وَإِذا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أَعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ وَقالُوا لَنا أَعْمالُنا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمالُكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause (سمعوا) is genitive through the adverb being put in construct with it; (اللغو) is the direct object; the clause (أعرضوا) has no grammatical position; (عنه) are attached to (أعرضوا); (قالوا) is conjoined to (أعرضوا); (لنا) is a khabar put first and (أعمالنا) a mubtadaʾ put after; and (لكم أعمالكم) is conjoined to what precedes. (سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لا نَبْتَغِي الْجاهِلِينَ): (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it [though indefinite] is permissible because it carries the sense of supplication; (عليكم) is the khabar. The salām here is a salām of farewell and leaving alone, not a salām of greeting and maintaining ties. The clause (لا نبتغي الجاهلين) is circumstantial; (لا) is negating; (نبتغي) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; and (الجاهلين) is the direct object. (إِنَّكَ لا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ): resumptive speech, set out to describe his eagerness for the faith of his uncle Abū Ṭālib. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا تهدي) is its khabar; the agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; (من) is the direct object and the clause (أحببت) the ṣila. In (ولكن الله) the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (يهدي) is its khabar; (من يشاء) is the direct object; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) the khabar; and (بالمهتدين) are attached to (أعلم).

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: The Muslims agree that this verse, «انك لا تهدي…», was revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib. When death came upon him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and said: "Uncle, say 'There is no god but Allah', a word by which I may argue for you before Allah." He said: "Son of my brother, I know that you are truthful, but I dislike that it be said he was alarmed at death. Were it not that there would be disgrace upon you [Translator's note: the text has «غليك», evidently a misprint for «عليك»] and upon the sons of your father, I would say it, and I would gladden your eye with it at parting, because of what I see of the intensity of your feeling and your sincere counsel." And he recited:
لولا الملامة أو حذار مسبة ... لوجدتني سمحا بذاك مبينا
(Were it not for blame, or fear of reproach, you would have found me ready to declare it openly.)
ولقد علمت بأن دين محمد ... من خير أديان البرية دينا
(I know well that the religion of Muḥammad is among the best religions of mankind.)
"But I shall die upon the creed of the elders, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Hāshim and ʿAbd Manāf." There are other, differing narrations that do not depart from this purport.

dervis-irab:14-17.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَاسْتَوى آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to continue the story of Joseph after his reaching full maturity «[Translator's note: so in the source, "Yūsuf"; the context is the story of Moses.]». (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or connective; that has preceded. (بلغ) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent, its implied form being "huwa", and (أشده) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The explanation of al-ashudd and the views about it have passed more than once. (استوى) is conjoined to (بلغ); what is meant is that his youth reached its end and his intellect was perfected. The clause (آتيناه) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (آتيناه) is a past verb, its agent and the first object; (حكما) is the second object and (علما) is conjoined to (حكما). (كذلك) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and (نجزي المحسنين) is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object. (وَدَخَلَ الْمَدِينَةَ عَلى حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ أَهْلِها): (ودخل المدينة) is conjoined to something omitted, i.e. "and he was absent from Pharaoh for a long time", because he stayed in Egypt thirty years, then went to Midian and stayed there ten years. (دخل المدينة) is a verb, its agent and an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). It is said that by the city is meant Munf, with ḍamma then sukūn, which is a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign; other things have also been said. (على حين غفلة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المدينة) or from the agent of (دخل), i.e. stealthily, and (من أهلها) is an adjective of (غفلة). It is said the time was between the two evening prayers; it is said it was the time of the midday nap; and it is said it was a feast day. The meaning of (على) here is adverbial (ẓarfiyya), i.e. "at the time". (فَوَجَدَ فِيها رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلانِ هذا مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ وَهذا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ): (فوجد) is conjoined to (دخل); (فيها) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (وجد); (رجلين) is the direct object, and the clause (يقتتلان) is an adjective of (رجلين). (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (من شيعته) a khabar (predicate), and the clause is a second adjective of (رجلين); it is also said to be a ḥāl — a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, which Sībawayh permitted without condition. (وهذا من عدوه) is conjoined to it. The Arabs point with (هذا) to one absent because it is the narration of a past state, so an absent past one is expressed with the demonstrative.
(فَاسْتَغاثَهُ الَّذِي مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ عَلَى الَّذِي مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (استغاثه) is a past verb and its direct object; (الذي) is the agent, and (من شيعته) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). (استغاث) is transitive by itself at times, as here, and at times with the bāʾ.
(فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسى فَقَضى عَلَيْهِ قالَ هذا مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ إِنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ مُضِلٌّ مُبِينٌ): (فوكزه) is also conjoined, i.e. he pushed him with his clenched fist; al-Kisāʾī said: he punched him. (موسى) is the agent. (فقضى عليه) is conjoined to (فوكزه). (قال) is a past verb and the clause is resumptive; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ and (من عمل الشيطان) a khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause (إنه عدو) is a reason. That does not impugn his infallibility, because it was an error and because it was unintended; he counted it only as the work of Satan, called it wrongdoing and sought forgiveness for it out of self-abasement and from regarding as grave the small slips that issue from them [i.e. the prophets]. (إن) and its noun, and (عدو) its khabar; (مضل) is an adjective and (مبين) a second adjective. (قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَغَفَرَ لَهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ):
(رب) is the one addressed (munādā), in genitive construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (ظلمت نفسي) is the khabar of (إن). (فاغفر لي): the fāʾ is conjunctive, (اغفر) is a verb of supplication, and (لي) is attached to (اغفر). (فغفر له) is conjoined. (إن) and its noun; (هو) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), (الغفور) the khabar and (الرحيم) a second khabar. It may also be parsed with (هو) as a mubtadaʾ and (الغفور الرحيم) as two khabars of (هو), the clause being the khabar of (إن).
(قالَ رَبِّ بِما أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيراً لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ): (بما): the bāʾ is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and the answer of the oath is omitted, its implied form being "I swear by Your favour upon me of forgiveness that I shall surely repent". (ما) is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ of the oath. The fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted answer. (لن) is a particle of negation, of the accusative and of the future; (أكون) is a defective imperfect verb, its noun latent, its implied form being "anā", and (ظهيرا) its khabar; (للمجرمين) is attached to (ظهيرا). The statement may also be an entreaty, as though he said: "My Lord, protect me, by the right of what You have bestowed upon me, from the disbelievers, and I shall never — if You protect me — be a supporter of the criminals." The bāʾ and what it governs are then attached to the implied "protect me", and it needs no answer; the fāʾ in (فلن أكون) is then the faṣīḥa, because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, as we mentioned. There are, moreover, other views, all sound, which we have reserved for the section on benefits.

* Benefits:
1- Continuation of the story of Moses:
Pharaoh took him as a son, and they sought wet-nurses for him, but he would not accept the breast of any one of them. When his whereabouts became unknown to his mother, her heart almost flew out of longing for him, so she sent his sister as though seeking a wet-nurse for him. When she saw their distress over him since he would not take to any wet-nurse, she said: «هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم», and they granted her request. She went and brought his mother — «وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها» — and she gave him her breast and he began to suckle it. She raised him in Pharaoh's palace. Then Āsiya presented him to Pharaoh, and when he took him, Moses stretched his hand to his beard and plucked it. Pharaoh said: "Bring me the slaughterers! This is he!" Āsiya said: "He is a delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him, for he is a child without understanding." She called for live coals and rubies for him, and Gabriel cast his hand into the fire; Moses put it in his mouth and it burned him, so Pharaoh left him. He grew up in his lap, and when he became a youth he adopted him, and he rode in his carriages, wore his clothes and was called the son of Pharaoh. Then Moses was told that Pharaoh had ridden out, so he rode after him and caught up with him in the town of Munf. He entered it when it had been cleared for Pharaoh and there was no one in its streets, and he saw an Israelite and a Copt fighting. The Israelite sought his help, so he struck the Copt and killed him. Their story then went as Allah the Exalted narrated in Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, until he went out fearful and watchful to Midian. The rest will come shortly.
2- The parsers' disagreement over «بما أنعمت عليّ»:
We have cited the two preferred analyses in parsing this verse, namely «قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين», and al-Zamakhsharī also chose them. He said: "By supporting the criminals he meant either the companionship of Pharaoh, being included in his company and swelling his ranks, since he used to ride when he rode, like a son with a father, and he was called the son of Pharaoh; or supporting one whose support led to crime and sin, like supporting the Israelite, which led to a killing that was not lawful for him." Likewise Abū al-Baqāʾ chose them in his book Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān. It is also said that this is not a statement but a supplication, i.e. "so let me not be, after this, a supporter", i.e. "so do not make me, O Lord, a supporter of the criminals".

dervis-irab:57-60.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا: إِنْ نَتَّبِعِ الْهُدى مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفْ مِنْ أَرْضِنا): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to what precedes, so it is in effect a branching from the story of Abū Ṭālib. They said: al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUthmān ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "We know that you are upon the truth, but we fear that if we follow you and oppose the Arabs, they will snatch us away from our land." (إن) is conditional; (نتبع) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), in the jussive (majzūm), and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we"; (الهدى) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (معك) is an adverb attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (نتخطف) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "we"; and (من أرضنا) are attached to (نتخطف). (أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَهُمْ حَرَماً آمِناً يُجْبى إِلَيْهِ ثَمَراتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ رِزْقاً مِنْ لَدُنَّا وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and the wāw is conjoined to something omitted that the context calls for. By it their claim, which has no basis of truth, is refuted: He established them in the Sanctuary, which He made secure by the sanctity of the House, and made its inhabitants secure by its sanctity. More on this meaning will come in the section on rhetoric. (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; (نمكن) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم), and the agent is latent, its implied form being "We"; (لهم) are attached to (نمكن); (حرما) is the direct object; (آمنا) is an adjective; and the clause (يجبى) is a second adjective of (حرما). The meaning of (يجبى إليه) is: is driven and carried to it and gathered for its flourishing. (إليه) are attached to (يجبى); (ثمرات كل شيء) is the deputy agent; (رزقا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of His saying (يجبى), because the meaning of jibāya (being gathered) and rizq (provision) is one, and what is meant is that provisions are driven to it. Others parsed it as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and al-Zamakhsharī allowed it, though one has some reservation about it. It may also be that (رزقا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of a passive participle, so it is accusative as a ḥāl from (الثمرات), since that is particularised by the construct (iḍāfa). (من لدنا) is an adjective of (رزقا); the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; (لكن أكثرهم) is lākinna and its noun, and the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar (predicate).
(وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَها): this may be resumptive speech, set out to make its people fear the evil outcome of those who were in a blessing, were ungrateful for it and met it with baṭar. Baṭar, with two fatḥas, is liveliness and insolence, lack of capacity to bear a blessing, bewilderment and perplexity, exceeding all bounds because of a blessing, and disliking a thing without its deserving dislike. The Qāmūs says: "The verb of all of these is like fariḥa; and baṭira al-ḥaqq is to be too proud for the truth and so not accept it." It may also be conjoined to what precedes so that the speech runs on consistently. (كم) is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a direct object put before (أهلكنا); (من قرية) is the tamyīz (specification) of the predicative kam, made genitive by (من) — its establishment has preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it; the clause (بطرت) is an adjective of (قرية); and (معيشتها) is accusative by removal of the preposition, after the pattern of His saying:
«واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا», i.e. "in its livelihood". This is the closest of what has been said about it and the least strained. Al-Zajjāj said it is accusative as an adverb of time, i.e. "the days of its livelihood". It is also permissible for (بطرت) to be made to contain the meaning of "lost", so that (معيشتها) would be a direct object; Abū al-Baqāʾ confined himself to this.
(فَتِلْكَ مَساكِنُهُمْ لَمْ تُسْكَنْ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ الْوارِثِينَ): in (فتلك) the fāʾ is a conjunction and (تلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (مساكنهم) is the khabar; the clause (لم تسكن) may be a second khabar, or it may be a ḥāl, the governor in it being the sense of pointing; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (قليلا) is an adverb, i.e. "except for a little time", so the exception is from the adverb; or it is an absolute object, i.e. "except for a little dwelling", so the exception is from the maṣdar; neither of the two views is preferable. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (كنا) is kāna and its noun; (نحن) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), also called ʿimād (support); and (الوارثين) is the khabar of (كنا). More on this meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ الْقُرى حَتَّى يَبْعَثَ فِي أُمِّها رَسُولًا يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِنا): resumptive speech, set out to state the custom of Allah the Exalted with His servants. (ما) is negating; (كان ربك) is kāna and its noun; (مهلك القرى) is its khabar; (حتى) is a particle of causation and genitive; (يبعث) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an an that is necessarily implied after (حتى); the agent is latent, referring to Allah; (في أمها) are attached to (يبعث); (رسولا) is the direct object; the clause (يتلو) is an adjective of (رسولا); (عليهم) are attached to (يتلو); and (آياتنا) is the direct object. What is meant by "its mother" is its greatest [town]; generalising here is better than restricting it to Mecca. (وَما كُنَّا مُهْلِكِي الْقُرى إِلَّا وَأَهْلُها ظالِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; kāna and its noun; (مهلكي القرى) is its khabar; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; the wāw is circumstantial; (أهلها) is a mubtadaʾ and (ظالمون) the khabar; and the clause is circumstantial. So the exception is from the most general of states, i.e. "We would not destroy them in any state at all except in the state of their being wrongdoers". (وَما أُوتِيتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَمَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وَزِينَتُها): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (ما) is a conditional noun that makes jussive, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أوتيتم) is a passive past verb, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the tāʾ is the deputy agent; (من شيء) is a ḥāl explaining (من) [Translator's note: so in the text, evidently for «ما»]; the fāʾ links the answer; (متاع) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; (الحياة) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (الدنيا) is an adjective; (زينتها) is conjoined to (متاع); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the verb [of the condition] and the answer are the khabar of (ما). (وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; (خير) is the khabar; (أبقى) is conjoined to (خير); the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ is conjoined to something omitted that the context calls for; (لا) is negating; and (تعقلون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) with its agent.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī):
In His saying «حرما آمنا» there is figurative attribution, because what is meant is the people of the Sanctuary; its discussion has preceded many times. Similar is «وكم أهلكنا من قرية», where what is meant is its people, as shown by His saying afterwards «فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن إلا قليلا», i.e. they had prided themselves on them for a time, false hopes deluded them, blessing made them insolent, and their way was the way of the luxurious who strut in the robes of happiness; then before long they perished, the days folded them away, and their remains were left standing, faded ruins and effaced traces, mocking them and showing others the folly of their judgment and the levity of their minds. Al-Mutanabbī glimpsed the sky of this lofty eloquence in his immortal ode in which he lamented Abū Shujāʿ Fātik, where he said his famous verse:
تتخلف الآثار عن أصحابها ... حينا ويدركها الفناء فتتبع
(Monuments outlast their owners for a while; then extinction overtakes them and they follow.)
He means that monuments, that is buildings, remain after their masters to show their power, strength and might; then there befalls them after them the same extinction that befell their owners, and ruin will overtake them, so the monuments go as those who made them went. This is the custom of the world with its people, and this is what is familiar of its vicissitudes. It is fitting that we present to you a choice selection of this ode, in keeping with our stipulation in this book:
الحزن يقلق والتجمل يردع ... والدمع بينهما عصيّ طيّع
(Grief unsettles and composure restrains, and between them the tear is both rebellious and obedient.)
يتنازعان دموع عيد مسهّد ... هذا يجيء بها وهذا يرجع
(The two contend over the tears of a sleepless eye: this one brings them and that one sends them back.) [Translator's note: the text has «عيد», evidently a misprint for «عين» (eye).]
النوم بعد أبي شجاع نافر ... والليل معي والكواكب ظلّع
(Sleep, after Abū Shujāʿ, shies away; the night is exhausted and the stars are limping.)
Ibn Jinnī said: "If the night and the stars were things on which grief could have an effect, his death would have affected them." Al-Khaṭīb said: "He only meant that the night is long because of losing him, so the night is exhausted and the stars limp and do not move." Al-Wāḥidī said: "Sleep after him does not keep company with the eye, so it does not sleep out of grief for him; and the night, from its length, is as though it had become too tired to walk and so stopped; and the stars are as though limping, unable to cross the sphere and set. With all this he describes his night after him, out of grief for him." Al-Wāḥidī said: Abū Shujāʿ Fātik died in Egypt on the night of Sunday, eleven nights gone of Shawwāl, in the year 350 AH.
Abū al-Ṭayyib went on to say:
إني لأجبن عن فراق أحبتي ... وتحس نفسي بالحمام فأشجع
(I am a coward at parting from my loved ones, yet my soul senses death and I am brave.)
ويزيدني غضب الأعادي قسوة ... ويلم بي عتب الصديق فأجزع
(The anger of enemies only makes me harder, but a friend's reproach comes upon me and I am distressed.)
تصفو الحياة لجاهل أو غافل ... عما مضى منها وما يتوقّع
(Life is clear only for one ignorant or heedless of what has passed of it and what is to be expected,)
ولمن يغالط في الحقائق نفسه ... ويسومها طلب المحال فتطمع
(and for one who deceives himself about realities and makes his soul seek the impossible, so it hopes.)
أين الذي الهرمان من بنيانه ... ما قومه؟ ما يومه؟ ما المصرع؟
(Where is he whose building the two Pyramids are? Who were his people? What was his day? What was his end?)
تتخلف الآثار … the verse [quoted above].

dervis-irab:18-21.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَصْبَحَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ خائِفاً يَتَرَقَّبُ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, and (أصبح) is a past verb, defective (nāqiṣ) or complete (tāmm). On the first view its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", (في المدينة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and (خائفا) the khabar (predicate) of (أصبح); or (في المدينة) is the khabar of (أصبح) and (خائفا) a ḥāl. On the second view the fāʿil (agent) of (أصبح) is latent, its implied form being "huwa", (في المدينة) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, and (خائفا) is a ḥāl. On both views the clause (يترقب) is a second ḥāl, or a second khabar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (خائفا), making it an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). The object of (يترقب) is omitted, i.e. he was watching for something disliked; it is unlikely that he was watching for relief, because the context makes that improbable.
(فَإِذَا الَّذِي اسْتَنْصَرَهُ بِالْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, and (إذا) is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the discussion of whether it is an adverb or a particle has preceded. (الذي) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (استنصره) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (بالأمس) is attached to (استنصره). The clause (يستصرخه) is the khabar of (الذي), and what (يستصرخه) attaches to is omitted, i.e. "against another Copt". (قالَ لَهُ مُوسى إِنَّكَ لَغَوِيٌّ مُبِينٌ): (قال) is a past verb, (له) is attached to it, and (موسى) is the agent. (إنك): (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (غوي مبين) are two khabars of (إن). (فَلَمَّا أَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يَبْطِشَ بِالَّذِي هُوَ عَدُوٌّ لَهُما): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or connective; (أن) is redundant (zāʾida), and its redundancy is regular after (لما) and before (لو) preceded by an oath, as in the poet's words:
فأقسم أن لو التقينا وأنتم ... لكان لكم يوم من الشر مظلم
(I swear: had we and you met, you would have had a day dark with evil.)
(أن) was added only to signal that Moses' haste to kill the second was not like his haste to kill the first; rather, there was a slowness in him in stretching out his hand to him, and the Qurʾān expressed that slowness by adding (أن). Something similar has preceded in Sūrat Yūsuf, in the words of the Exalted «فلما أن جاءه البشير ألقاه على وجهه», so refresh your memory of it.
(أراد) is a past verb, and (أن) and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar as the object of (أراد). (بالذي) is attached to (يبطش); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (عدو) a khabar and (لهما) an adjective, and the clause is the ṣila of (الذي). (قالَ يا مُوسى أَتُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقْتُلَنِي كَما قَتَلْتَ نَفْساً بِالْأَمْسِ): (قال) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "huwa", referring to the Israelite who sought help; he said that thinking that Moses wanted to strike him. It is also said that it refers to the Copt, and that is not far-fetched; Zādah preferred it in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī, as though [the Copt] inferred from Moses' rebuke of the Israelite that he was the one who killed the man the day before. (أتريد): the hamza is for the interrogative of denial, and (تريد) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (أن) and what falls within its scope is the object of (تريد). (كما قتلت) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, and parallels to it have preceded; (نفسا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (بالأمس) is attached to (قتلت). (إِنْ تُرِيدُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ جَبَّاراً فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِينَ): (إن) is negating; (تريد) is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent, its implied form being "anta"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and (أن) and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar as the object of (تريد). (جبارا) is the khabar of (تكون), and (في الأرض) is an adjective of (جبارا). (وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين) is conjoined to the similar preceding clause. (وَجاءَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعى): the wāw conjoins to something omitted that is inferred from the context of the speech, i.e. "So the Copt who heard what the Israelite said, and knew that Moses was the killer of the first Copt, went to Pharaoh and informed him of the plain facts; Pharaoh became angry and ordered Moses to be killed and arrested." (جاء رجل) is a verb and its agent; he was a believer from Pharaoh's household, referred to elsewhere in the Qurʾān; it is said he was Pharaoh's cousin. (من أقصى المدينة) is an adjective of (رجل), and the clause (يسعى) is a second adjective, or a ḥāl, because (رجل) has been specified by the description, as the well-known rule is. (من أقصى المدينة) may also be attached to (جاء), in which case the clause (يسعى) is only an adjective.
(قالَ يا مُوسى إِنَّ الْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَاخْرُجْ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ): (إن الملأ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يأتمرون) is the khabar; (بك) is attached to (يأتمرون), i.e. they are consulting together. Al-iʾtimār is consultation; one says "the two men yataʾāmarān and yaʾtamirān" with one meaning, because each of them commands his companion to do something or advises him on a matter. It is also said that its meaning is that they command one another to kill you, and perhaps this is clearer. The author of al-Tāj cited both meanings; he said: "Iʾtamarū and taʾāmarū: they consulted together; and iʾtamarū bi-fulān: they intended [harm] to him and commanded one another to kill him." (بك) is attached to (يأتمرون). (ليقتلوك): the lām is of reason, and the imperfect is accusative (manṣūb) by a concealed (أن) after it. (فاخرج): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you heed my advice, then go out". (إني) is a reason for his command to go out: (إن) and its noun, and (لك) is attached to an omitted ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to this and disallowed attaching it to (الناصحين), but others permitted that it be attached to (الناصحين) because of the latitude allowed with adverbial phrases, or to what the word (الناصحين) indicates, i.e. "an adviser to you, among the advisers". (فَخَرَجَ مِنْها خائِفاً يَتَرَقَّبُ قالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so Moses acted on his advice and went out". (منها) is attached to (خرج), (خائفا) is a ḥāl, and the clause (يترقب) is a second ḥāl. The object of (يترقب) is omitted, i.e. evil, or their overtaking him; it is also said: he was watching for Allah's help, but the first is more fitting to the context. (رب) is the one addressed (munādā); (نجني) is a verb of supplication, and the yāʾ is the direct object; (من القوم) is attached to (نجني), and (الظالمين) is an adjective.

dervis-irab:61-64.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ وَعَدْناهُ وَعْداً حَسَناً فَهُوَ لاقِيهِ كَمَنْ مَتَّعْناهُ مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and the fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the disapproval of equality between the people of this world and the people of the Hereafter follow upon what precedes it, namely the evident disparity between the two sides. (من) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (وعدناه) is its ṣila (relative clause), and (كمن) is its khabar (predicate). (وعدناه) is a verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وعدا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (حسنا) an adjective; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (لاقيه) the khabar. The kāf is a noun meaning "like", the khabar; or it is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the khabar. The clause (متعناه) is the ṣila of (من); (متاع الحياة الدنيا) is an absolute object; (ثم) is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ; (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached (mutaʿalliq) to (المحضرين); and (من المحضرين) is the khabar of (هو). Al-Zamakhsharī has a useful discussion analysing this verse from the point of view of i'rab, which we present here: "If you say: Explain to me the two fāʾs and ثم, and tell me their positions, I say:
In the verse before it He mentioned the enjoyment of the life of this world and what is with Allah, and their disparity; then He followed it with His saying أفمن وعدناه, in the sense: Is it, after this evident disparity, that one equates the sons of the Hereafter with the sons of this world? This is the meaning of the first fāʾ and the statement of its position. As for the second, it is for causation, because meeting what was promised is caused by the promise, which is the guarantee of good. As for ثم, it is for the remoteness of the state of being brought [for punishment] from the state of being given enjoyment, not for the remoteness of its time from its time."
(وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ): the adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember", and the speech is resumptive. The clause (يناديهم) is genitive through the adverb being put in construct (iḍāfa) with it; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He", referring to Allah, and the hāʾ is the direct object. The purpose of this calling is rebuke and reproach. (فيقول) is conjoined to (يناديهم); (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted khabar put first; (شركائي) is a mubtadaʾ put after; (الذين) is an adjective of (شركائي); the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (الذين); kāna and its noun, and the clause (تزعمون) is its khabar. The two objects of (تزعمون) are omitted, their implied form being "you claim them to be My partners". The omission of the two objects of ẓanantu and its sisters will be mentioned in the section on benefits. The clause (أين شركائي) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(قالَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ رَبَّنا هؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَغْوَيْنا أَغْوَيْناهُمْ كَما غَوَيْنا): resumptive speech, set out to answer an implied question, as though it were said: "So what came from them then?" (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (حق عليهم) is the ṣila; (القول) is the agent; (ربنا) is a muḍāf vocative (munādā) from which the vocative particle is omitted; (هؤلا) [Translator's note: so in the text, for «هؤلاء»] is a mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is an adjective of (هؤلاء); the clause (أغوينا) is the ṣila; the clause (أغويناهم) is the khabar of (هؤلاء); and (كما أغوينا) [Translator's note: so in the text; the Quranic wording is «كما غوينا»] is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "we led them astray, so they went astray with an erring like our erring". In this parsing we have followed what al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān parsed.
(تَبَرَّأْنا إِلَيْكَ ما كانُوا إِيَّانا يَعْبُدُونَ): the clause is explicative, confirming what precedes it. (تبرأنا) is a past verb and its agent; (إليك) are attached to (تبرأنا); (ما) is negating; kāna and its noun; (إيانا) is an object put before (يعبدون); and the clause (يعبدون) is the khabar of (كانوا). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed (ما) to be maṣdariyya, with the maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from what they used to worship", i.e. from their worshipping us. I see no need for this strain, because the meaning is "they did not worship us; rather they worshipped their own desires and gave free rein to their lusts". (وَقِيلَ ادْعُوا شُرَكاءَكُمْ فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (قيل) is a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "this saying", in mockery of them and to silence them; (ادعوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (شركاءكم) is the direct object. In (فدعوهم) the fāʾ is a conjunction and (دعوهم) is a past verb, its agent and direct object. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (يستجيبوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and the wāw is the agent; and (لهم) are attached to (يستجيبوا).
(وَرَأَوُا الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا يَهْتَدُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (رأوا العذاب) is a past verb, its agent and direct object; (لو) is conditional; (أن) and what follows it is the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "if their being guided in this world had been established, they would not have seen the punishment in the Hereafter"; (أن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; kāna and its noun, and the clause (يهتدون) is its khabar.

* Benefits:
By the consensus of the grammarians it is permissible to omit the two objects of ẓanantu and its sisters among the verbs of the heart, for brevity (ikhtiṣāran), when there is evidence indicating them, as in «أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون», and the saying of al-Kumayt praising the Family of the House:
بأي كتاب أم بأية سنة ... ترى حبهم عارا عليّ وتحسب
(By which Book, or by which Sunna, do you consider loving them a disgrace upon me, and so reckon it?)
In the verse the two objects of تزعمون were omitted, and in the line the two objects of تحسب, because what precedes them indicates them, i.e. "you claim them to be partners" and "you reckon loving them a disgrace upon me". As for omitting one of the two for brevity when there is evidence, the majority allowed it, as in His saying, Exalted is He, «ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم», its implied form being "and let not those who are miserly reckon what they are miserly with to be good for them", so the first object was omitted because it is indicated; and as in the saying of ʿAntara:
ولقد نزلت فلا تظني غيره ... مني بمنزلة المحب المكرم
(You have taken, so do not think otherwise, the place of the beloved and honoured one with me.)
Its implied form is "so do not think other than it to be the case from me", so the second object was omitted. The tāʾ in نزلت has kasra, and the ḥāʾ and rāʾ of المحب المكرم have fatḥa.
In the fifth chapter of al-Mughnī there is an explanation that a thing may be thought to be a case of omission when it is not: The grammarians' habit has been to say that the object is omitted ikhtiṣāran (for brevity) and iqtiṣāran (by restriction), meaning by ikhtiṣār omission because of evidence and by iqtiṣār omission without evidence, and they exemplify it [Translator's note: the text has «ينحو», evidently for «بنحو»] with «كلوا واشربوا», i.e. "perform these two acts", and the saying of the Arabs about a verb that takes two objects: "whoever hears, imagines", i.e. "a supposing arises from him". The precise statement is that one should say: Sometimes the purpose concerns giving information merely about the occurrence of the act, without specifying who did it or to whom it was done, so its maṣdar is brought attributed to a verb of general being, and one says "a fire occurred" or "a plundering". Sometimes it concerns giving information merely about the agent's doing of the act, so one restricts oneself to these two and the object is neither mentioned nor intended — since what is intended is like what is stated — and it is not called omitted, because for this purpose the verb is treated as one having no object. Of this kind are: «ربي الذي يحيي ويميت», «هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون», «كلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا», «وإذا رأيت ثم», since the meaning is: my Lord is He who does giving life and causing death; are one who is characterised by knowledge and one from whom knowledge is absent equal?; perform eating and drinking and leave extravagance; and when seeing arises from you there. Of it also, on the more correct view, is «ولما ورد ماء مدين» to the end of the verse. Do you not see that he, upon him be blessing and peace, only pitied the two women because they were in the state of holding back while their people were in the state of watering, not because what they held back was sheep and what the people watered was camels? Likewise what is intended in their saying «لا نسقي» [is the watering], not the thing watered. Whoever has not reflected supplied: "they water their camels", "the two hold back their sheep", "we do not water our sheep". And sometimes what is intended is to attribute the act to its agent and attach it to its object, so both are mentioned, as in «لا تأكلوا الربا», «ولا تقربوا الزنا», and your saying "how good Zayd is!". In this kind, if its object is not mentioned, it is said to be omitted, as in «ما ودعك ربك وما قلى». And there may be something in the wording that calls for it, so that one is certain it must be supplied, as in «أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا», «وكل وعد الله الحسنى» and:
حميت حمى تهامة بعد نجد ... وما شيء حميت بمستباح
(You protected the preserve of Tihāma after Najd, and nothing you have protected is ever made lawful to others.)

dervis-irab:65-70.t:
* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ: ماذا أَجَبْتُمُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ؟): speech conjoined to what precedes it. They were asked first about their associating partners [with Allah], and asked second about their answer to the messengers who forbade them from that. (فيقول) is conjoined to (يناديهم).
