(ماذا) as a whole is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), not a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because ajāba does not pass to a second object by itself but through the bāʾ, and dropping the preposition is not according to rule; the meaning is "with what kind of answer did you answer them?". (المرسلين) is the direct object of (أجبتم). (فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَنْباءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَهُمْ لا يَتَساءَلُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (عميت عليهم الأنباء) is a verb and its agent — the discussion of attributing blindness to the tidings will come in the section on rhetoric. (يومئذ) is an adverb put in construct (iḍāfa) with one like it, and the tanwīn in (يومئذ) is a compensation for a clause, i.e. "the day when they were called and it was said to them: With what did you answer the messengers?". In (فهم) the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (لا يتساءلون) the khabar (predicate). (فَأَمَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً فَعَسى أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُفْلِحِينَ): resumptive speech, set out to state the condition of the believers after stating the condition of the unbelievers. (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (من) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause (تاب) is the ṣila (relative clause); (عمل صالحا) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object, or an absolute object, i.e. "did a righteous deed"; the fāʾ is linking; (عسى) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope that work like kāna; its noun is latent, its implied form being "he", and (أن) and what falls within its scope is its khabar. Hope from the generous is equivalent to certainty; or the hope is in its proper sense, but on the part of the one who repents. (من المفلحين) is the khabar of (يكون). (وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ وَيَخْتارُ ما كانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (ربك) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يخلق) the khabar; (ما) is the direct object and (يشاء) the ṣila; (يختار) is conjoined to (يخلق); (ما) is negating; (كان) is a past incomplete verb; (لهم) is its khabar put first and (الخيرة) its noun put after; and the clause is explicative, because it confirms what precedes it; it may also be resumptive. It has been said that (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. "He chooses their choosing", the maṣdar standing in the place of the passive participle, i.e. "what they choose". It has been said that (ما) is a relative meaning "that which", with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "that in which they had the choice". It has also been said that (كان) is complete (tāmma), and the clause (لهم الخيرة) is resumptive speech. (سبحان الله) is an absolute object of an omitted verb; (تعالى) is a past verb whose agent is "He"; (عما) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تعالى); and the clause (يشركون) is the ṣila.
(وَرَبُّكَ يَعْلَمُ ما تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ربك) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يعلم) the khabar; (ما) is the direct object and (تكن) the ṣila; (صدورهم) is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) is conjoined to the first (ما), and the clause (يعلنون) is the ṣila. (وَهُوَ اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْأُولى وَالْآخِرَةِ وَلَهُ الْحُكْمُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الله) the khabar; the clause (لا إله إلا هو) is a second khabar — the i'rab of the formula of divine unity and the disagreement about it have preceded. (له) is a khabar put first and (الحمد) a mubtadaʾ put after, and the clause is a third khabar; (في الأولى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (الآخرة) is conjoined to (الأولى); (إليه) are attached to (ترجعون); (ترجعون) is a passive imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
1- Attributing blindness to the tidings is a rational metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī), which has preceded many times. What is meant is that the tidings became as though blind and could not find their way to them. It has been said that it is a case of inversion (qalb), its original form being "so they became blind to the tidings"; and inversion, as has preceded, is one of the embellishments of speech.
2- Embedding (al-idmāj):
In His saying «له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة» there is idmāj. Its definition is that the speaker embeds either one purpose in another purpose, or one figure in another figure, in such a way that only one of the two purposes or one of the two figures appears in the speech, while the other is embedded in the purpose present in the speech. In this verse hyperbole has been embedded in antithesis (al-muṭābaqa), because His being alone, Glorified is He, in praise in the Hereafter — which is the time in which none but He is praised — is hyperbole in describing His Essence as alone and praised. And although the speech in these two outwardly takes the form of hyperbole, the matter in it is inwardly literal truth, because He is the most worthy of praise in the two abodes and the Lord of praise, thanks and fair commendation in both places in reality, while anyone else among all His creation is praised in this world only figuratively, and the reality of his praise goes back to the Master of praise, Glorified is He.

dervis-irab:22-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تِلْقاءَ): Mention has already been made of the maṣdars (verbal nouns) that come on this pattern; the meaning here is direction.
(مَدْيَنَ): a town in Egypt «[Translator's note: so in the source.]» lying on the Sea of al-Qulzum opposite Tabūk; in it is the well from which Moses drew water. Madyan is also the name of a tribe mentioned by Yāqūt. Al-Jalāl said: "It is the village of Shuʿayb, eight days' journey from Egypt, named after Madyan son of Abraham; and he did not know the way to it."
(سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): its middle and the main part of its course; it is of the type in which the adjective is put in genitive construct with the qualified noun, i.e. the middle road.
(تَذُودانِ): the two of them were driving their sheep away from the water. Of this usage are the poet's words:
أبيت على باب القوافي كأنما ... أذود بها سربا من الوحش نزّعا
(I spend the night at the door of rhymes, as though I were driving off with them a herd of wild beasts eager [for water].)
(ما خَطْبُكُما): what is your situation? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its literal meaning is: what is your makhṭūb, i.e. your aim in driving [the flock] off? The thing aimed at was called khaṭb just as the thing intended is called shaʾn in your saying 'mā shaʾnuka?' One says shaʾantu shaʾnahu, i.e. I aimed at his aim." In al-Qāmūs and its commentary: "Al-khaṭb is a maṣdar, and [it means] the situation; one says 'mā khaṭbuka?', i.e. what is your situation and what drove you to it. Al-khaṭb is a matter, small or great, and its use has come to predominate for a great, disliked matter." This root has many meanings, to be sought in the large lexicons, and because they are so many someone versified these meanings, saying:
ومرّة الوعظ تسمى خطبة ... ثم التماس للنكاح الخطبة
وما به يخطب فهو الخطبة ... وحمرة أي في سواد الشعر
فحمرة في كدرة تدعى خطب ... وخطبة النكاح جمعها خطب
وجمع خطبة بمنبر خطب ... والخطب سهل أي سبيل الأمر
فالأمر مع صرف الزمان خطب ... والخطبة الخاطب كل خطب
جمع لأخطب وخطبا خطب ... في كل ذي اختلاف لون يجري
وفي الوعظ قل وفي النكاح خطبا ... نعم وفي كدرة لون خطبا
وإن ترد صار خطيبا خطبا ... أتى بسجع في الكلام النثر
(A didactic poem listing the vowelings and meanings of the root kh-ṭ-b: khuṭba, an exhortation; khiṭba, a marriage proposal; khuṭba, a reddish tinge in black hair; khaṭab, redness mixed with dullness of colour; the plurals khuṭab and khiṭab; khaṭb, a matter or calamity brought by the turns of time; khuṭb as plural of akhṭab; the verb forms khaṭaba for preaching and proposing, khaṭiba for a dull colour, and khaṭuba, to become an eloquent preacher using rhymed prose.)
(يُصْدِرَ الرِّعاءُ): al-ṣadr from a thing is returning from it; of its verb one says ṣadara, of the patterns of naṣara and ḍaraba. Al-ṣadar, with two fatḥas, is a noun of the maṣdar from it. It is transitive by itself, so one says ṣadarahu ghayruhu, i.e. someone else made him return, i.e. turned him back; and it is used in the four-letter form, so one says aṣdarahu ghayruhu. Al-riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿin, irregularly, because the regular plural of the adjective of the pattern fāʿil whose final radical is weak, like qāḍin, is fuʿala, like quḍāh and rumāh — in disagreement with al-Zamakhsharī's saying that it is the plural of rāʿin on the pattern fiʿāl, regularly, like ṣiyām and qiyām. As for the plural fiʿāl, it is regular in six types, which we set out below:
1- A noun or an adjective whose middle radical is not yāʾ, on the pattern faʿl or faʿla. The noun: like kaʿb and kiʿāb, thawb and thiyāb, nār and niyār, qaṣʿa and qiṣāʿ, janna and jinān; the adjective: like ṣaʿb, ṣaʿba and ṣiʿāb, ḍakhm, ḍakhma and ḍikhām. It rarely comes from one with a weak middle radical, like ḍayʿa and ḍiyāʿ, ḍayf and ḍiyāf.
2- A noun with a sound final radical, not doubled, on the pattern faʿal or faʿala, like jamal and jimāl, jabal and jibāl, raqaba and riqāb, thamara and thimār.
3- A noun on the pattern fiʿl, like dhiʾb and dhiʾāb, ẓill and ẓilāl, biʾr and biʾār.
4- A noun on the pattern fuʿl whose middle radical is not wāw and whose final radical is not yāʾ, like rumḥ and rimāḥ, rīḥ and riyāḥ, duhn and dihān. As for al-dihān in the words of the Exalted «فكانت وردة كالدهان», it will come that it is a singular noun whose meaning is red leather.
«[Translator's note: rīḥ is listed under this pattern as in the source.]»
5- An adjective with a sound final radical on the pattern faʿīl or faʿīla, like karīm, karīma and kirām, marīḍ, marīḍa and mirāḍ, ṭawīl, ṭawīla and ṭiwāl.
6- An adjective on the pattern faʿlān, or faʿlā, or faʿlāna, or fuʿlāna «[Translator's note: the source writes the same unvocalised pattern فعلانة twice; the examples show faʿlāna and fuʿlāna.]», like ʿaṭshān, ʿaṭshā and ʿiṭāsh, rayyān, rayyā and riwāʾ, nadmān, nadmā and nidām, khumṣān, khumṣāna and khimāṣ.
Whatever is pluralised on fiʿāl apart from what has been mentioned is irregular, and that is like rāʿin, rāʿiya and riʿāʾ; qāʾim, qāʾima and qiyām; ṣāʾim, ṣāʾima and ṣiyām; aʿjaf, ʿajfāʾ and ʿijāf; khayyir and khiyār; jayyid and jiyād; jawād and jiyād; abṭaḥ and biṭāḥ; qalūṣ and qilāṣ; unthā and ināth; nuṭfa and niṭāf; faṣīl and fiṣāl; sabuʿ and sibāʿ; ḍabuʿ and ḍibāʿ; nufasāʾ and nifās; ʿusharāʾ and ʿishār.
We do not know how this escaped al-Zamakhsharī, so that he said in his Kashshāf: "As for al-riʿāʾ with kasra, it is regular, like ṣiyām and qiyām."
(اسْتِحْياءٍ): al-istiḥyāʾ and al-ḥayāʾ are modesty, reserve and withdrawal. Al-Miṣbāḥ says: "One says istaḥaytu with one yāʾ, and with one yāʾ, and with two yāʾs «[Translator's note: "with one yāʾ" is repeated in the source.]»; and it is transitive by itself and with the particle, so one says istaḥyaytuhu and istaḥyaytu minhu."
(الْقَصَصَ), with two fatḥas: a maṣdar in the sense of the thing narrated, and it later came to be used as a name for the thing narrated. One says qaṣṣa ʿalayhi al-khabar, he told him the news, and its maṣdar is qaṣaṣ with two fatḥas; as for al-qiṣaṣ with kasra on the qāf, it is the plural of qiṣṣa.

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقاءَ مَدْيَنَ قالَ عَسى رَبِّي أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِي سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): the wāw is resumptive; (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or connective; (توجه) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa". (تلقاء مدين) is an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to (توجه). (تلقاء) is used as a maṣdar, as a noun for meeting, and as a place for it. We mentioned previously that we have ten maṣdars that came irregularly with kasra on their first letter. The commentator on al-Qāmūs made it a noun of the maṣdar, saying in commenting on al-Qāmūs: "His words 'and the noun is al-tilqāʾ', i.e. the noun of the maṣdar — but this is disturbed by his saying 'it has no parallel except al-tibyān', since no one has said that al-tibyān is a noun of the maṣdar; rather it is a rare maṣdar." The wording of al-Muḥkam: "Al-tilqāʾ is a noun of the maṣdar, not a maṣdar, otherwise the tāʾ would have fatḥa; it is also said to be a maṣdar with no parallel except al-tibyān." (مدين) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and it is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine. The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (عسى) is an inflexible past verb among the verbs of hope; (ربي) is its noun, and (أن) and what falls within its scope is its khabar (predicate). (سواء السبيل) is a second object, or accusative by removal of the preposition. (وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِنَ النَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ): (وجد) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "huwa"; (عليه) is attached to (وجد), because (وجد) means "met"; (أمة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. a dense crowd; (من الناس) is a naʿt (adjective) of (أمة), and the clause (يسقون) is a second adjective or a ḥāl (circumstantial). The object of (يسقون) is omitted because it is known, i.e. their livestock. (وَوَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِمُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودانِ): (وجد) is conjoined to the first (وجد); (من دونهم) is also attached to (وجد), i.e. in a place below them; (امرأتين) is the first object «[Translator's note: so in the source, "first object", though no second object is named.]», and the clause (تذودان) is an adjective of (امرأتين). (قالَ ما خَطْبُكُما قالَتا لا نَسْقِي حَتَّى يُصْدِرَ الرِّعاءُ وَأَبُونا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ): (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (خطبكما) is the khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (قالتا) is a past verb; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, voweled with fatḥa to suit the alif of the dual, and the alif is the agent; the clause (لا نسقي) is the object of their saying. (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive, and (يصدر) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by a concealed (أن) after (حتى); (الرعاء) is the agent. The wāw is circumstantial; (أبونا) is a mubtadaʾ, (شيخ) a khabar and (كبير) an adjective. The secret of the circumstantial clause will come in the section on rhetoric. (فَسَقى لَهُما ثُمَّ تَوَلَّى إِلَى الظِّلِّ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted and implied, understood from the context of the speech. (سقى) is a past verb, (لهما) is attached to it, and the direct object is omitted, i.e. their sheep, for their sake. (ثم) is a conjunction; (تولى) is a past verb, and (إلى الظل) is attached to (تولى), i.e. to the shade of a tree that was there. (فَقالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ): (رب) is the one addressed (munādā); (إن) and its noun. (لما): the lām is a preposition, and (ما) is an indefinite noun meaning "a thing", or a relative noun, i.e. "for whatever thing" or "for that which You have sent down"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (فقير). (أنزلت) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is either an adjective of (ما) if it is indefinite, or a ṣila (relative clause). (إليّ) is attached to (أنزلت); (من خير) is a ḥāl, and (فقير) is the khabar of (إن). (فقير) was made transitive with the lām because it was made to include the meaning of "asking" or "seeking"; otherwise it is transitive with (إلى).
(فَجاءَتْهُ إِحْداهُما تَمْشِي عَلَى اسْتِحْياءٍ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "So the two returned to their father in less time than they used to spend in watering; he asked them the reason for that, and they told him the story of the one who watered for them; he said to one of them, 'Call him to me,' so she came to him." (إحداهما) is the agent; the clause (تمشي) is a ḥāl from the agent, and (على استحياء) is a ḥāl from the agent concealed in (تمشي), i.e. modest and shy. It is also said: covering her face with the sleeve of her shift out of modesty before him.
(قالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ ما سَقَيْتَ لَنا): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يدعوك) is the khabar. (ليجزيك): the lām is of reason, and (يجزيك) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām of reason; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يدعوك). The kāf is the first object and (أجر) the second object. (ما) is maṣdariyya, and it and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar in genitive construct with (أجر), i.e. "the wage for your watering". (لنا) is attached to (سقيت).
(فَلَمَّا جاءَهُ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ الْقَصَصَ قالَ لا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, the implied form being: "So he answered her — not to take the wage, but to seek blessing from her father, since he had heard from the two of them that he was a very old man. She walked ahead of him, and the wind began to strike her garment and uncover her shins — or the wind pressed her garment against her body and revealed its shape — so he said to her: 'Walk behind me and guide me on the way.' She did so until he came in to him." (فلما جاءه وقص عليه): (قص) is a past verb; (عليه) is attached to (قص), and (القصص) is the direct object. The clause (قال) has no grammatical position. (لا) is prohibitive and (تخف) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا). (نجوت) is a verb and its agent; (من القوم) is attached to (نجوت), and (الظالمين) is an adjective. He calmed his fear and reassured him only because Midian was not under Pharaoh's authority.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ījāz (concision):
Concision abounds in these verses. The direct object has been omitted in four places: the first is the object of (يسقون), i.e. their livestock; the second is the object of (تذودان), i.e. their [two women's] livestock; the third is (لا نسقي), i.e. our livestock; and the fourth is (فسقى لهما), i.e. their livestock. The reason for the omission is that the purpose is to make known that there was watering by the people and driving-off by the two girls, that they said "لا نسقي", i.e. there will be no watering by us until the shepherds depart, and that there was watering by Moses. As for whether what was watered was sheep or camels or something else, that is a matter outside the scope of the purpose.
2- Kināya (metonymy):
In His words «وأبونا شيخ كبير»: they wanted to say to him: "We are two weak, sheltered women; we cannot jostle with men, and we have no man to do that, and our father is an old man advanced in years whom age has weakened and exhausted. So we have no alternative but to leave the watering and postpone it until the people have finished their needs with the water." Thus their answer matched his question, because he asked them the reason for the driving-off and they said what they said. It was permissible for Allah's prophet Shuʿayb to accept for his daughters the menial work of watering livestock, despite the exposure and loss of reserve it involves, only because necessities make prohibited things permissible — although the matter in itself is not prohibited, for religion does not reject it, customs differ, and the way of the people of the desert is other than the way of the townspeople, especially when the situation is one of necessity.
3- Ishāra (allusion):
That is in His words «على استحياء». With a flashing glimpse like the blink of an eye, and in a language that is the language of the gaze, He alluded to a description of her splendid, captivating beauty through [the word] modesty, because shyness is one of the qualities of beautiful women, and because a slow, swaying gait is among their most prominent traits. Al-Aʿshā said:
كأن مشيتها من بيت جارتها ... مر السحابة لا ريث ولا عجل
(Her walk from her neighbour's house is like the passing of a cloud, neither slow nor hasty.)
And Ibn al-Rūmī created as excellently as excellence allowed him when he said:
جرت تدافع من وشي لها حسن ... تدافع الماء في وشي من الجب
(She moved, surging in a fine embroidered robe of hers, as water surges in an embroidery of ripples.)
«[Translator's note: the ending «من الجب» is as printed; it may be a misprint for «من الحبب» (ripples/bubbles), which the gloss follows.]»
And whether he [thereby] glimpsed the heaven of Imruʾ al-Qays in his words «[Translator's note: the phrase «وان رمق سماء امرئ القيس» is elliptical in the source; rendered literally.]»:
سموت إليها بعد ما نام أهلها ... سمو حباب الماء حالا على حال
(I rose up to her after her people had slept, rising as bubbles of water rise, state after state.)
And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa in his marvellous ode rhyming in rāʾ:
فلما فقدت الصوت منهم وأطفئت ... مصابيح شبت بالعشي وأنور وغاب قمير كنت أرجو غيابه ... وروّح رعيان وهوّم سمر
وخفض عني الصوت أقبلت مشية ... الحباب وركني خيفة القوم ازور
(When I no longer heard their voices, and the lamps and fires lit at dusk were put out, and the little moon whose setting I hoped for had set, and the herdsmen had returned and the night-talkers dozed, and the voices around me were lowered, I came forward with the gait of a gliding serpent, my side bent away for fear of the people.)

dervis-irab:71-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَرْمَداً): sarmad is the continuous, unbroken. Scholars differed over its derivation. It has been said that it is from sard, which is succession, with the mīm added, its pattern being faʿmal, as in dulāmiṣ from dilāṣ — one says dirʿ dilāṣ, i.e. a smooth, strong coat of mail. This is what al-Zamakhsharī and others preferred. The author of the Qāmūs and some grammarians chose that the mīm is radical and its pattern faʿlal, because the addition of mīm in the middle and at the end is not according to regular rule.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ اللَّيْلَ سَرْمَداً إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): the hamza is for interrogation; (رأيتم) is a verb and its agent, i.e. "tell me"; (إن) is conditional; (جعل الله عليكم) — (جعل) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (الله) is the fāʿil (agent); (عليكم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (الليل) is the first object of (جعل) and (سرمدا) its second object; (إلى يوم القيامة) is an adjective of (سرمدا). (أرأيتم) has been suspended (ʿulliqat) from governing because of the interrogative. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, supplied according to what the context calls for, its implied form being "then tell me".
(مَنْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِضِياءٍ أَفَلا تَسْمَعُونَ): the interrogative clause is in the position of accusative as the object of (أرأيتم). (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (إله) the khabar (predicate); (غير الله) is an adjective of (إله); the clause (يأتيكم) is a second adjective of (إله); (بضياء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يأتيكم). In (أفلا) the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the fāʾ is conjoined to something omitted and implied; (لا) is negating; and (يسمعون) [Translator's note: so in the text; the Quranic wording is «تسمعون»] is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the agent.
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ النَّهارَ سَرْمَداً إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ مَنْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِلَيْلٍ تَسْكُنُونَ فِيهِ أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ): its i'rab has preceded.
(وَمِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): (من رحمته) is a khabar put first, and (جعل لكم) is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by supplying an, a mubtadaʾ put after. This is frequent in their speech, and of it is the proverb:
تسمع بالمعيدي خير من أن تراه (That you hear of the Muʿaydī is better than that you see him.)
(جعل) is a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (لكم) is the second object of (جعل) and (الليل) the first object of (جعل); (النهار) is conjoined to (الليل). He paired [Translator's note: the text has «زواج», evidently for «زاوج»] the two for a subtle point whose details will come in the section on rhetoric. In (لتسكنوا) the lām is for causation and (تسكنوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām, and the wāw is the agent; (فيه) are attached to (تسكنوا); (لتبتغوا من فضله) is conjoined to (لتسكنوا); (لعلكم) is laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (تشكرون) is its khabar.
(وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ): its i'rab, in the same wording, preceded recently, so renew your acquaintance with it. (وَنَزَعْنا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً فَقُلْنا هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, so that the speech runs on consistently; (نزعنا) is a verb and its agent, i.e. "We brought out"; (من كل أمة) are attached to (نزعنا); (شهيدا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فقلنا) is conjoined to (نزعنا); the clause (هاتوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (هاتوا) is an imperative verb and its agent, and (برهانكم) is the direct object. (فَعَلِمُوا أَنَّ الْحَقَّ لِلَّهِ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (علموا) is a past verb and its agent; (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (علموا); (أن) and its noun, and (لله) is its khabar; (ضل) is a past verb; (عنهم) are attached to (ضل); (ما) is the agent; the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); kāna and its noun, and the clause (يفترون) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Correspondence (al-munāsaba):
In His saying «أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا» up to His saying «أفلا تبصرون» there is the figure of munāsaba. It is of two kinds: correspondence in meanings and correspondence in words. The semantic kind is that the speaker begins with a meaning and then completes his speech with what corresponds to it in meaning, not in wording. When He, Glorified is He, attributed to Himself making the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection — He being the Powerful who, when He makes a thing, none other can oppose it — He said «أفلا تسمعون», because hearing corresponds to the dark side, in that the night is suited to hearing rather than seeing, since sight does not penetrate darkness. And when He attributed to Himself making the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, as though no night at all had been created in it, He said at the end (fāṣila) of this verse «أفلا تبصرون», because of the correspondence between day and seeing.
As for verbal correspondence, its discussion will come in this book.
2- Folding and unfolding (al-laff wa-l-nashr):
There is laff and nashr in His saying «ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون». The discussion of this figure has preceded, and we mentioned that it consists of mentioning several things, in detail or in summary, and then mentioning what belongs to each one of them without specifying, trusting that the hearer will distinguish what belongs to each and refer it to what it belongs to. He paired the night and the day for three purposes: first, that you may rest in one of them, namely the night; and that you may seek of [His] bounty in the second, namely the day; and to will your thankfulness. This is among the most delightful things with which a speaker displays skill, in prose or verse.
3- Correctness of correspondences (ṣiḥḥat al-muqābalāt):
In this verse there is also a figure that they have defined as ṣiḥḥat al-muqābalāt. It consists of the speaker's taking care to arrange his speech as it should be: when he brings at its beginning certain things, he matches them at its end with their opposites, or with things other than them, contrasting or agreeing, in order, so that the first is matched with the first and the second with the second, and nothing of that is broken in the contrasting or the agreeing. Whenever he breaks the order, the speech is defective in correspondence. This verse is among the inimitable instances of this category: night and day came at the beginning of the speech, and they are opposites; rest and movement came at its end, and they are opposites; and each side is matched with the other side in order. He, Glorified is He, expressed movement with a word of "consequence" (irdāf), so the speech entailed a kind of beauty in addition to the correspondence. What required turning from the word "movement" to the expression "seeking bounty" is that movement may be for benefit or for harm, while seeking bounty is movement for benefit, not harm; and it involves the joining of help with strength, and good choice that indicates soundness of intellect and of the senses; and it entails the illumination of the side in which that particular movement occurs, so that the one who moves may be guided to attaining his aims and the ways of benefit and may guard against the causes of ruin. The verse was set out to enumerate blessings, so it was necessary to turn from the word "movement" to a word that is its consequence and follower, so that the beauty of expression might be complete. Thus these words, which are part of a verse, contain a number of benefits and advantages which, if enumerated with the words coined for them, would need many words to express. So by this speech, for this reason, several kinds of beauty were achieved. Do you not see that He, Glorified is He, made the cause of the existence of night and day the attainment of man's benefits, where He said «لتسكنوا» and «لتبتغوا» with the lām of causation? These words have gathered correspondence, causation, allusion (ishāra), consequence (irdāf), harmony (iʾtilāf), good sequence and good expression, because the speech in them comes closely knit, its parts holding one another by the neck. Then He informed with the truthful report that all the blessings He enumerated, which are of the two kinds, allusion and consequence, are part of His mercy, where He said with the partitive particle «ومن رحمته». And all this is in part of a verse numbering eleven words. So observe this evident eloquence and mutually supporting purity of speech.
4- Explanation (al-tafsīr):
In His saying «ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون» [Translator's note: so in the text, without «والنهار»] there is the figure of tafsīr, which is that you mention things and then explain them with what corresponds to them. Of it is the saying of Ibn Ḥayyūs:
ومقرطق يغني النديم بوجهه ... عن كأسه الملأى وعن إبريقه
(Many a youth in a tunic spares the drinking companion, by his face, the need for his full cup and his ewer;)
فعل المدام ولونها ومذاقها ... في مقلتيه ووجنتيه وريقه
(the effect of wine, its colour and its taste are in his eyes, his cheeks and his saliva.)

dervis-irab:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(قالَتْ إِحْداهُما يا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ): (قالت إحداهما) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); she was the elder, whom Moses later married. The parsing of (يا أبت) has preceded many times. (استأجره) is an imperative verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is a reason for the command before it; the meaning of this comprehensive and exclusive (jāmiʿ māniʿ) statement will come in the section on rhetoric. (إن), its noun and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (استأجرت) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (القوي) is the first khabar (predicate) and (الأمين) the second khabar. (قالَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنْكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ابْنَتَيَّ هاتَيْنِ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أريد) is its khabar, the clause being the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (أن أنكحك) is an interpreted maṣdar as the object of (أريد). The agent of (أنكحك) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anā"; the kāf is the first object and (إحدى ابنتي) the second object; (ابنتي) is in genitive construct with (إحدى), and (هاتين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ابنتي). The demonstrative is to distinguish the two of them from the rest of their sisters, for he had, as is narrated, seven daughters. (عَلى أَنْ تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمانِيَ حِجَجٍ): (على) is a preposition that has entered upon (أن) and what follows it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [element] in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the agent or from the object, i.e. "that being stipulated upon me" or "upon you". (تأجرني) is an imperfect verb from ajartuhu, "when you were a hired man for him", like your saying abawtuhu, i.e. "I was a father to him". The second object of (تأجرني) is omitted, i.e. "yourself". (ثماني حجج) is an adverb [of time] for (تأجرني), ḥijaj being years. Al-Zamakhsharī contrived an analysis — I do not know how it held up for him — namely that (ثماني) is the second object of (تأجرني); he needed to imply a muḍāf, i.e. "the herding of eight years", and there is no call for this contrivance. That is besides the fact that the meaning does not hold up with it, because it is the work for which reward is given, not the time; so how can the hire be directed to the time?
(فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْراً فَمِنْ عِنْدِكَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional, and (أتممت) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (عشرا) is the direct object. The fāʾ connects the apodosis because it is a nominal clause. (من عندك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the completion is from you", and there is no obligation or compulsion in the matter.
(وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negating; (أريد) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "anā"; (أن) and what falls within its scope is the object of (أريد); (عليك) is attached to (أشق). (ستجدني) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the agent being latent, its implied form being "anta"; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ the direct object. The clause (إن شاء الله) is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the apodosis of (إن) is omitted. (من الصالحين) is attached to (تجدني). The meaning of (أشق عليك) is: make the matter difficult. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the literal meaning of 'shaqaqtu ʿalayhi' and 'shaqqa ʿalayhi al-amr'? I say: its literal meaning is that when a matter is too great for you, it is as though it split your opinion in two: at one time you say 'I can bear it' and at another 'I cannot bear it'." More on that will come in the section on rhetoric.
(قالَ ذلِكَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ وَاللَّهُ عَلى ما نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (بيني وبينك) its khabar, i.e. "that which you have covenanted with me and stipulated to me stands firm and established between us, and neither of us will deviate from it". (أيما الأجلين):
(أي) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of (قضيت), and (ما) is redundant (zāʾida) for vagueness. An extensive study of (أي) will come in the section on benefits. It is also said that (ما) is an indefinite noun meaning "a thing", and (الأجلين) is a badal (substitute) from it. (قضيت) is a verb and its agent. The fāʾ connects the apodosis; (لا) is the lā of generic negation, and (عدوان) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; (علي) is the khabar of (لا). (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (على ما نقول) is attached to (وكيل), and (وكيل) is the khabar of (الله).

* Rhetoric:
1- The comprehensive and exclusive statement (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ):
In the words of the Exalted «إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين». In this verse there are numerous devices, and for that reason the scholars of rhetoric have described it as belonging to comprehensive, exclusive, wise speech to which nothing can be added. For when these two qualities — competence and trustworthiness — are combined in the one who manages your affairs and looks after your concerns, your mind is at rest, your affair is complete and your aim is made easy. And because it has taken the course of a coined proverb, so that it goes on through the passing ages and the coming eras. In it there is generalisation, which is more beautiful and more fitting in women's praise of men than specific praise, and more preserving of decorum and reserve — especially after she had understood her father's purpose, namely marrying her to him. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to admire this expression and aim at its heights in his supplication, saying: "I complain to Allah of the weakness of the trustworthy and the treachery of the strong."
This indirection (īhām) on the part of Shuʿayb's daughter was also followed by Zulaykhā with Joseph — but how far apart are innate modesty and affected modesty! "Eyes made up with kohl are not like [eyes with natural] kohl." For she said: «ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم», meaning: what is the recompense of Joseph for the evil he intended toward me except that you imprison him or punish him with a painful punishment? But she made her husband imagine modesty and shyness, and that she would speak of chastity while depravity was attributed to her, intimating that it was this modesty of hers that prevented her from speaking of this matter of Joseph's seduction — all the more and with greater reason. So in this verse, as you have seen, there is concision, proverb, generalisation and indirection. In it too there is fronting: what more deserved to be fronted was fronted and made the noun of (إن), namely (خير); and it came with the wording of the past verb to indicate that the matter is not novel, and that it is known and settled, having been tried and become customary. Of exquisite fronting are the words of Abū al-Shaghb al-ʿAbsī grieving over Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qasrī when Yūsuf ibn ʿAmr «[Translator's note: so in the source; the governor is usually named Yūsuf ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafī.]» took him captive:
ألا إن خير الناس حيا وهالكا ... أسير ثقيف عندهم في السلاسل
(Indeed the best of people, alive or perished, is the captive of Thaqīf, with them in chains.)
لعمري لئن عمرتم السجن خالدا ... وأوطأتموه وطأة المتثاقل لقد كان نهّاضا بكل ملمة ... ومعطي اللهى غمرا كثير النوافل
(By my life, if you have made Khālid dwell in prison and made him tread with the tread of one weighed down, he used to rise swiftly to every calamity, and give gifts abundantly, with many bounties.)
(خير الناس) is an elative (ism tafḍīl) in genitive construct with what is made definite by al-, and it is the noun of (إن); (حيا وهالكا) are two ḥāls from it, and (أسير ثقيف) is the khabar of (إن). Thaqīf is the proper name of the tribe, and a proper name is more definite than what is adorned with al-; so the khabar of (إن), in genitive construct with it, is more definite than its noun, which is in genitive construct with what is adorned with al-; the noun was fronted out of concern for it. (عندهم في السلاسل) is a ḥāl, or a khabar after a khabar. (لعمري) is an oath. (إن عمرتم), i.e. if you have entered Khālid into prison and made him dwell there; (أوطأتموه), i.e. you made him tread the ground with his foot like the tread of the heavy-laden, i.e. one carrying something heavy, because of the fetter put on his feet, so it is a kināya (metonymy) for that. (لقد كان نهاضا) is the answer of the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, i.e. he was quick to rise to every heavy calamity. And he was a giver of al-lahā — with fatḥa, the plural of lahāh, like ḥaṣā and ḥaṣāh, i.e. the flesh at the back of the mouth, but here in the sense of the mouth itself; it may also be al-luhā, with ḍamma on the lām, the plural of luhwa, like ghuraf and ghurfa, meaning a gift of whatever kind.
2- Ījāz (concision):
In His words «وما أريد أن أشق عليك» there is eloquent concision, for we have mentioned the meaning of "shaqqa ʿalayhi al-amr" and that it wavers between despair and hope. In it is an allusion to those harsh people who burden their workers with tasks exceeding their capacity and going beyond the bounds of their known ability. On this the revealed laws have proceeded: good dealing and taking the easier and lighter way. Of it is the ḥadīth: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was my partner, and he would not dodge, nor quarrel, nor dispute."

* Benefits:
(أيّ) with doubling:
(أيّ) with doubling comes in five ways:
1- To be conditional, as in «أيما الأجلين قضيت»; (ما) may be added after it for emphasis.
2- To be interrogative: «أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا».
3- Relative: «ثم لننزعنّ من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا».
4- To indicate the meaning of perfection, so it occurs as an adjective of an indefinite noun, as in "Zayd is a man, ayyu rajulin", i.e. perfect in the qualities of men; and as a ḥāl from a definite noun, as in "I passed by ʿAbd Allāh, ayya rajulin". Abū al-ʿAtāhiya said, where it occurs as an adjective:
إن الشباب والفراغ والجده ... مفسدة للمرء أي مفسده
(Youth, leisure and wealth are a corruption for a man — what a corruption!)
5- To be a link to the vocative of what has al-, as in "yā ayyuhā al-rajul".
The author of al-Mughnī cited a verse of Abū al-Ṭayyib containing (أي), namely:
أي يوم سررتني بوصال ... لم ترعني ثلاثة بصدود
(What day did you gladden me with union without frightening me for three with aversion?)
He said: "(أي) in it is not relative, because the relative is put in genitive construct only with a definite noun. Abū ʿAlī said in al-Tadhkira about the words:
أرأيت أي سوالف وخدود ... برزت لنا بين اللوى فزرود
(Did you see what necks and cheeks appeared to us between al-Liwā and Zarūd?)
(أي) in it cannot be relative, because it is in genitive construct with an indefinite noun." The author of al-Mughnī continued his words, saying: Nor is it conditional, because the meaning would then be "if you gladden me one day with your union, you make me safe for three days from your aversion", and this is the reverse of the intended meaning. Rather it is for an interrogative by which negation is meant, as when you say to one who claims he honoured you: "What day did you honour me?" The meaning is: you never gladdened me one day with your union without frightening me for three with your aversion. The first clause is resumptive, its adverb fronted because it has the right to the front; the second is either in the position of the genitive as an adjective of (وصال), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "you did not frighten me after it", just as it was omitted in the words of the Exalted «واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس» (the verse); or accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (سررتني) or its object, the meaning being "what day did you gladden me without frightening me" or "without [my] being frightened by you", it being an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), like the one in «طبتم فادخلوها خالدين»; or it has no grammatical position, on the view that it is conjoined to the first by an omitted fāʾ, as was said about «وإذ قال موسى لقومه إن الله يأمركم أن تذبحوا بقرة قالوا: أتتخذنا هزوا قال أعوذ بالله» and likewise in the rest of the verse — but that is far-fetched; the precise scholars hold regarding the verse that the clauses are resumptive, with the implied [questions]: "So what did they say to him?" "So what did he say to them?" Whoever narrates (ثلاثة) in the nominative cannot, in his view, have the ḥāl be from the agent of (سررتني), because (ترعني) lacks a pronoun referring to the possessor of the ḥāl.
Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī said in his commentary on the Dīwān of al-Mutanabbī: "(أي) is accusative, and it is an interrogative used in the sense of negation, as you say to one who claims he honoured you: 'What day did you ever honour me?', as al-Hudhalī said:
اذهب فأي فتى في الناس أحرزه ... من حتفه ظلم دعج ولا جبل
(Go! For what youth among people have pitch-dark shadows or a mountain ever guarded from his death?)
(أي) cannot be conditional, linking clause to clause as the apodosis is linked to the protasis; if you take it as conditional, it contradicts the meaning he intended, as though he were saying: 'If you gladden me one day with your union, you make me safe for three from your aversion', and this is the reverse of what he meant."
This verse is among the amatory verses with which Abū al-Ṭayyib opened an ode he composed in his youth. We cite the amatory verses here because of their preciousness, and we parse some of what is useful in them:
كم قتيل كما قتلت شهيد ... ببياض الطّلى وورد الخدود
(How many a slain one, slain as I was, a martyr to white necks and rosy cheeks,)
وعيون المها ولا كعيون ... فتكت بالمتيم المعمود
(and to the eyes of wild cows — yet none like the eyes that have murdered the love-enslaved, the love-sick one.)
درّ درّ الصّبا أأيام تجر.... ير ذيولي بدار أثلة عودي
(How abundant the bounty of youth! O days of trailing my skirts in the abode of Athla, return!)
عمرك الله هل رأيت بدورا ... طلعت في براقع وعقود
(By your life, I ask Allah — have you seen full moons rising in veils and necklaces,)
راميات بأسهم ريشها الهد.... ب تشقّ القلوب قبل الجلود
(shooting arrows feathered with eyelashes that split the hearts before the skins?)
يترشّفن في فمي رشفات ... هن فيه أحلى من التوحيد
(They sip from my mouth sips that are sweeter in it than [the formula of] tawḥīd —)
كلّ خمصانة أرقّ من الخم.... ر بقلب أقسى من الجلمود ذات فرع كأنما ضرب العن.... بر فيه بماء ورد وعود حالك كالغداف مثل دجو.... جيّ أثيث جعد بلا تجعيد تحمل المسك عن غدائرها الري.... ح وتفتّر عن شتيت برود جمعت بين جسم أحمد والسق.... م وبين الجفون والتسهيد أهل ما بي من الضنى بطل صي.... د بتصفيف طرّة وبجيد كل شيء من الدماء حرام ... شربه ما خلا دم العنقود
(every slender-waisted one, more delicate than wine, with a heart harder than rock; with tresses as though ambergris had been beaten into them with rosewater and aloes-wood, jet-black like the raven, like the dark of night, thick and curly without curling; the wind carries musk from her braids, and she smiles to reveal well-spaced, cool teeth. She has joined the body of Aḥmad [the poet] with sickness, and his eyelids with sleeplessness. Worthy of the emaciation I suffer is a proud champion [felled] by an arranged forelock and a neck. Every kind of blood is forbidden to drink except the blood of the grape-cluster;)
فاسقنيها فدى لعينيك نفسي ... من غزال وطارفي وتليدي
(so give it to me to drink — may my soul be ransom for your eyes, O gazelle, and my newly gained and inherited wealth.)
شيب رأسي وذلتي ونحو لي ... ودموعي على هواك شهودي
(The greying of my head, my abasement, my emaciation and my tears are my witnesses to my love for you.)
أي يوم سررتني ... (البيت) («What day did you gladden me…» — the verse [cited above].)
The parsing of some words:
(كم) is predicative (khabariyya), and its tamyīz (specification) is genitive by construct with it or by (من); the discussion of it has preceded at length. Here it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (ببياض). (كما قتلت) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. They have, moreover, a long discourse on passionate love (ʿishq), and its account is reasonable among the masters of Sufism. Al-Junayd said: "Passionate love is a merciful affinity and a yearning inspiration which the generosity of Allah has made incumbent on every being with a spirit, so that through it may be attained the supreme delight, the like of which cannot be attained except through that affinity. It exists in souls, its ranks measured according to their possessors; so there is no one but is passionately in love with something by which the degree of his rank among creation may be inferred. For that reason the noblest ranks in this world are the ranks of those who renounced it though it was before their eyes, and inclined to the Hereafter though it was hidden from them." Allah the Exalted has described Himself with love, saying: «يحبهم ويحبونه», and the discussion of it has preceded at length. As for ʿishq, it has not occurred in the language of the revealed law. Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said beautiful words, among them: "If Allah the Exalted granted me one answered supplication, I would supplicate Him, the Exalted, to forgive the passionate lovers, because their movements are compelled, not chosen." How excellent are the words of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī:
وكم في الناس من حسن ولكن ... عليك لشقوتي وقع اختياري
(How many beautiful ones there are among people! But, to my misery, my choice fell on you.)
A man of the Arabs said to one of the Banū ʿUdhra: "What is it with one of you dying of passionate love in his longing for a woman he has grown attached to? That is nothing but weakness of soul or a feebleness you find in yourselves, O Banū ʿUdhra!" He said: "By Allah, if you had seen the long, fine eyebrows above the dark-black eyes, beneath which are the gap-toothed smiles, you would have taken them as al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā!" «[Translator's note: the source's closing quotation mark follows this anecdote; its opening mark at al-Fuḍayl's words is not matched.]» Abū al-Ṭayyib relied, in his word (شهيد), on a ḥadīth they narrate: "Whoever loves passionately, remains chaste and conceals it, and then dies, dies a martyr."
(عمرك الله): a maṣdar. One says "aṭāla Allāhu ʿumraka" and "ʿamraka", with ḍamma and with fatḥa. Although both are maṣdars with one meaning, one of them — the one with fatḥa on the ʿayn — is used in oaths. When you put the lām of inception on it, you make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, the implied form being "la-ʿamru Allāhi [is] my oath". If you do not bring the lām, you put it in the accusative as maṣdars are, and say "ʿamra Allāhi I did not do such-and-such" and "ʿamraka Allāha I did not do such-and-such", as though you said "by your affirming Allah", i.e. by your acknowledging Him as everlasting. Of it are the words of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
أيها المنكح الثّريا سهيلا ... عمرك الله كيف يلتقيان
(O you who marry al-Thurayyā to Suhayl — by your life, I ask Allah — how can the two meet?)
He means: I asked Allah to lengthen your life. In Abū al-Ṭayyib's words it is a maṣdar, and its meaning is: I asked Allah to grant you long life.
(أحلى من التوحيد): al-Wāḥidī said: "They used to suck my saliva because of their love for me, and the sips in my mouth were sweeter than the word of tawḥīd, which is 'There is no god but Allah'; and this is excess and transgression of bounds."
Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said: Many people hold that the expression "afʿal than such-and-such" necessitates preferring the first over the second in all places, and that is an error. The correct view is that afʿal comes in the speech of the Arabs in five ways. The first: that the first is of the same kind as the second, and no ruling has appeared for either of them by which it exceeds the other with an excess established by proof from the side of preference; this is literal in [expressing] superiority, not figurative, as when you say "Zayd is more excellent than ʿAmr" and "this sword is sharper than that one".
The second: that the first is of the same kind as the second, or close to it and capable of being joined to it, while a ruling has previously been established for the second that necessitated its excess by clear proof; this is by way of approximation in simile, not preference, as when you say "the prince is more generous than Ḥātim and braver than ʿAmr". The verse of al-Mutanabbī is of this kind, i.e. they sip from my mouth sips that are close to tawḥīd.
The third: that the first is of the same kind as the second, or close to it, while the second is below the first; this is by way of pure information, as when you say "the sun is brighter than the moon" and "the lion is bolder than the leopard".
The fourth: that the first is not of the same kind as the second, while a ruling has previously been established for the second that produced «[Translator's note: the source has أوجد, "produced", where the parallel second case has أوجب, "necessitated".]» its excess, and the first is renowned among its own kind for excellence; this is by way of pure simile, the purpose being that the first attains some of what the second attains, as when you say "Zayd is braver than the lion and sharper than the sword".
The fifth: that the first is not of the same kind as the second, and the first is far below the second in the quality; this is by way of pure hyperbole, as in "his stature is more perfect than the spear" and "his face is brighter than the sun". In the ḥadīth it has come: "The dusty earth has not carried, nor has the green sky shaded, anyone more truthful in speech than Abū Dharr." One who does not know the meanings of speech held that Abū Dharr is the most truthful of the whole world, and the matter is not so; rather, he (upon him be blessing and peace) negated that anyone was of a higher rank than him in truthfulness. Had he meant what they held, he would have said: "Abū Dharr is more truthful than everyone whom [the sky] has shaded and [the earth] has carried."
(كل خمصانة): the nominative is permissible in it as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in (يترشفن), and on this (أرق) is nominative, following (كل). (كل) may also be accusative, taken as an adjective of his word (بدورا) or as a badal from it. Al-khumṣāna is the slender one; the masculine is khumṣān.
(أهل ما بي من الضنى بطل): (أهل) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (بطل), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: "I am worthy of what I suffer and deserving of it, and I am a proud champion."
(ما خلا دم العنقود): when you say "jāʾa al-qawmu mā khalā Zaydan", there is nothing but the accusative, because (خلا) must be a verb owing to the entry of the maṣdariyya (ما) upon it. When you say "jāʾa al-qawmu khalā Zaydin", it is the genitive and nothing else.

dervis-irab:29-32.t:
* I'rab:
(فَلَمَّا قَضى مُوسَى الْأَجَلَ وَسارَ بِأَهْلِهِ آنَسَ مِنْ جانِبِ الطُّورِ ناراً): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that is understood from the context, the implied form being: "So the contract between them for the hire and the marriage was concluded, and he carried out the task entrusted to him in the best and most perfect way; then when…". (لما) is temporal (ḥīniyya) or connective, and the clause (قضى موسى الأجل) has no grammatical position. (سار) is conjoined to (قضى); (بأهله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (سار). The clause (آنس) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (من جانب الطور) is attached to (آنس), and (نارا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). You may make (من جانب الطور) a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was an adjective of (نارا) and was placed before it. (قالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إِنِّي آنَسْتُ ناراً): (لأهله) is attached to (قال); the clause (امكثوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause (إني) is a reason for the command to stay. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (آنست) is its khabar (predicate); (نارا) is the direct object.
(لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ): the clause of hope is a ḥāl, i.e. "hoping". (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (آتيكم) is its khabar; the kāf is the direct object. (منها) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of (خبر); (بخبر) is attached to (آتيكم). (أو) is a conjunction, and (جذوة) is conjoined to (خبر). It has the jīm with any of the three vowels: a flame of fire, or a piece of firewood; its plural is jidhan. Ibn Muqbil said:
باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها ... جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا ذعر
(Laylā's wood-gatherers spent the night seeking for her thick firebrands, neither weak nor brittle.)
(من النار) is a naʿt (adjective) of (جذوة). The clause of hope is also a ḥāl: (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (تصطلون) is its khabar. (فَلَمَّا أَتاها نُودِيَ مِنْ شاطِئِ الْوادِ الْأَيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that the context requires, i.e. "so he went toward it, and when he came to it". The clause (نودي) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (من شاطئ الوادي) is attached to (نودي); (الأيمن) is an adjective of (شاطئ); (في البقعة) is a ḥāl from (الشاطئ), and (المباركة) is an adjective of (البقعة). (من الشجرة) is a badal (substitute) from His words (من شاطئ الوادي), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because the tree was growing on the bank. Its counterpart has preceded in His words «لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم», i.e. the call came to him from the bank of the valley from the direction of the tree.
(أَنْ يا مُوسى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ): (أن) is explicative, because calling is saying, the implied form being "that is: O Moses". Abū al-Baqāʾ and others permitted that it be lightened from the heavy [anna], its noun omitted and explained by the vocative clause, i.e. "he was called with [the fact] that it — i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) —". (إني): (إن) and its noun, with kasra on the hamza by agreement of the readers, because calling is saying. (أنا) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الله) is the khabar of (إن), or the khabar of (أنا) with the clause being the khabar of (إن). (رب العالمين) is an adjective of (الله) or a badal from it. (وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصاكَ فَلَمَّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّها جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِراً وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): the wāw is conjunctive and (أن) is explicative, conjoined to the preceding one. (ألق) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta", and (عصاك) is the direct object. (فلما): the fāʾ conjoins to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "so he threw it and it became a serpent". (رآها) is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause (تهتز) is circumstantial, and the clause (كأنها جان) is a ḥāl from the agent of (تهتز): (كأن) and its noun, and (جان) its khabar. The clause (ولى) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the agent of (ولى) is latent, its implied form being "huwa", and (مدبرا) is a ḥāl. The wāw is conjunctive, and the clause (لم يعقب) is conjoined to (ولى), i.e. "and did not return". (يا مُوسى أَقْبِلْ وَلا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ): (أقبل) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "anta". (ولا تخف): (لا) is prohibitive and (تخف) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا). (إن) and its noun, and (من الآمنين) its khabar; the clause is a reason for the command to come forward and the prohibition of fear. (اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ): (اسلك يدك) is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (في جيبك) is attached to (اسلك), from salaka al-shayʾa fī al-shayʾ, "he passed the thing into the thing". (تخرج) is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request, its agent latent, its implied form being "hiya"; (بيضاء) is a ḥāl, and (من غير سوء) is attached to (بيضاء). The reasoning for that has preceded in Sūrat Ṭā Hā, so refresh your memory of it. (وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ مِنَ الرَّهْبِ): Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you ask: what is the meaning of His words «واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب»? I say: There are two meanings in it. One of them is that when Moses (upon him be peace) turned the staff into a serpent, he was frightened and agitated and shielded himself from it with his hand, as one who fears a thing does. So it was said to him: Your shielding yourself with your hand is a humiliation before the enemies; so when you throw it, as soon as it turns into a serpent, put your hand under your upper arm in place of shielding yourself with it, then bring it out white, so that two things are achieved: avoiding what is a humiliation for you, and displaying another miracle. What is meant by the wing is the hand, because a person's two hands are in the position of a bird's two wings; and when he puts his right hand under the upper arm of his left hand, he has drawn his wing to himself. The second is that by drawing his wing to himself is meant his steeling himself, his self-control and his firmness when the staff turned into a serpent, so that he would not be agitated or afraid. It is borrowed from the action of the bird, because when it is frightened it spreads its wings and lets them hang loose; otherwise its wings are drawn to it, tucked in.
Of it is what is told of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: a secretary of his was writing before him when he involuntarily broke wind. He was ashamed and crestfallen, so he got up and struck the ground with his pen. ʿUmar said to him: 'Take your pen, draw your wing to yourself and let your fright be dispelled, for I have not heard it from anyone more than I have heard it from myself.'"
(اضمم) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "anta"; (إليك) is attached to (اضمم); (جناحك) is the direct object. (من الرهب) is attached to (اضمم), standing as its reason, i.e. "because of the fear". It is also said [to be attached] to (ولى), i.e. he fled out of fright; it is also said [to be attached] to (مدبرا); and it is also said [to be attached] to something omitted, i.e. "be calmed from the fear". Al-rahab is with fatḥa on the rāʾ and the hāʾ, and with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ. More detail will come in the section on rhetoric.
(فَذانِكَ بُرْهانانِ مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you have contemplated that and become certain of it, then those two…". (ذانك) is a demonstrative, the dual of (ذاك). Whoever read (ذانّك) with doubling made it the dual of (ذلك) with the lām of distance, the doubling being a compensation for it. (برهانان) is the khabar; (من ربك) is an adjective of (برهانان), i.e. "sent from your Lord"; (إلى فرعون) is attached to "sent", and (ملئه) is conjoined to (فرعون). The clause (إنهم) is a reason for sending the two proofs: (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; (كان) and its noun, and (قوما) its khabar, and (فاسقين) is an adjective of (قوما).

* Rhetoric:
Most of the rhetorical devices in these verses have preceded, such as istiʿāra (metaphor) and iḥtirās (precaution). We add to what has preceded what Imam al-Zamakhsharī set out in his enchanting style; this is its text: "If you ask: the wing, which is the hand, has been made in one of the two places the thing drawn, and in the other the thing drawn to — namely His words «واضمم إليك جناحك», and in Ṭā Hā «واضمم يدك إلى جناحك» — so how are they reconciled? I say: what is meant by the wing that is drawn is the right hand, and what it is drawn to is the left hand, and each of the right and the left of the two hands is a wing."
Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "If you ask: why was the proof (ḥujja) called burhān? I say: because of its whiteness and its illuminating, from their saying of a fair-skinned woman 'barahraha', with repetition of both the ʿayn and the lām [of the root]." This is a subtle reasoning which none but this imam could have deduced so well. Its meaning is that the nūn in al-burhān is augmentative; they say abraha al-rajul, when he brings a proof. Its counterpart is their also calling the proof sulṭān, from al-salīṭ, which is oil, because of its illuminating. In the lexicons: "abraha: he brought a proof, or wonders, and overcame people." This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī and the precise scholars. The author of al-Qāmūs claimed in one of his two views that the nūn is radical; he said: "barhana ʿalayhi: he established the proof; and al-burhān, with ḍamma, is the proof." So reflect.

* Benefits:
The staff of Moses again:
We presented in Sūrat Ṭā Hā an extensive study of the staff, and we add here what relates specifically to the staff of Moses. History narrates that Shuʿayb had the staffs of the prophets with him, and he said to Moses at night: "Enter that room and take a staff from those staffs." He took a staff with which Shuʿayb was infatuated — and he was blind — so he was reluctant to part with it and said: "Another one." But nothing fell into his hand except it, seven times, so he knew that it had a special significance. It is also said that Shuʿayb ordered his daughter to give Moses a staff with which to drive the wild beasts away from his sheep, and it fell into her hand seven times, as preceded. In the books of tafsīr there are curiosities about that staff for which there is no room in our book.

dervis-irab:76-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ): i.e. the band (ʿuṣba) is weighed down by them, in going to pains to rise with them. More on the inversion (qalb) in this expression will come in the section on rhetoric. One says nāʾa, yanūʾu, nawʾan and tanwāʾan: he rose with effort and hardship; nāʾa bihi al-ḥiml: the load weighed him down and made him lean; nāʾa al-najm: the star set in the west with the dawn while another rose opposite it at that very hour in the east. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Nāʾa, yanūʾu, nawʾan, with hamza, of the pattern of qāla: he rose." And in the Qāmūs:
nāʾa bi-l-ḥiml: he rose heavily with the load; nāʾa bihi al-ḥiml: the load weighed him down and made him lean, like anāʾahu; and nāʾa fulān: he was weighed down and fell — a word with opposite meanings (ḍidd).
(المفاتح): the plural of miftāḥ (key); it ought properly to have been pluralised as mafātīḥ, but this yāʾ may be dropped, just as they sometimes bring in a yāʾ in a plural that has no yāʾ. It has been said that mafātiḥuhu is the plural of miftaḥ, so there is no omission in it.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ قارُونَ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسى): resumptive speech, set out to mention the story of Qārūn and the admonitions and lessons it contains. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb, and (قارون) is its noun. It is a foreign proper name like Hārūn, a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign; had it been of the pattern fāʿūl from qarana it would have been fully declinable. His story will come shortly. The clause (كان) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), referring to Qārūn; and (من قوم موسى) is the khabar of (كان), i.e. he was his paternal cousin or his maternal cousin, and believed in him, as will come. (فَبَغى عَلَيْهِمْ وَآتَيْناهُ مِنَ الْكُنُوزِ ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ أُولِي الْقُوَّةِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (بغى) is a past verb whose agent is latent, referring to Qārūn; (عليهم) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to (بغى) [Translator's note: the text has «بيبغى»]; (آتيناه) is a past verb, its agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من الكنوز) are attached to (آتيناه); (ما) is a relative noun, the second direct object of (آتيناه); (إن) is a particle resembling the verb and (مفاتحه) is the noun of (إن). In (لتنوء) the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (تنوء) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "they" (hiya), referring to the keys (al-mafātiḥ), plural of miftaḥ with kasra, which is that with which one opens; and the clause is the khabar of (إن). The clause (إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (بالعصبة) are attached to (تنوء), and (أولي القوة) is an adjective of (العصبة). (إِذْ قالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ): the adverb is attached to (تنوء); it has been said, to an implied "remember". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is an adverb of (آتيناه); it may also be an adverb of an omitted verb indicated by the speech, i.e. 'he transgressed when his people said to him'." The clause (قال) is in the position of genitive through the adverb being put in construct (iḍāfa) with it; (له) are attached to (قال); (قومه) is the fāʿil (agent); the clause (لا تفرح) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (لا) is prohibitive and (تفرح) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the agent of (تفرح) is latent, its implied form being "you". The clause (إن الله) gives the reason for the prohibition — the secret of this giving of reason will come in the section on rhetoric. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يحب الفرحين) is its khabar.
(وَابْتَغِ فِيما آتاكَ اللَّهُ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ وَلا تَنْسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيا): the wāw is a conjunction; (ابتغ) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; (في) is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya or relative; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "moving about in what He has given you"; the sense of «في» here is causation. The clause (آتاك الله) has no grammatical position; (آتاك الله) is a past verb, a direct object put first and an agent put after. (الدار) is the object of (ابتغ) and (الآخرة) an adjective of (الدار). In (ولا تنس), (لا) is prohibitive and (تنس) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا), its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (نصيبك) is the direct object; (من الدنيا) are attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl. "Portion" is what suffices you, meets your need and sets your affairs right; further discussion of the portion and what is meant by it will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَأَحْسِنْ كَما أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ وَلا تَبْغِ الْفَسادَ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أحسن) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; (كما) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "do good like the good with which Allah has done good to you"; (إليك) are attached to (أحسن); (ولا تبغ الفساد) is conjoined to what precedes; (في الأرض) are attached to (الفساد) or to (تبغ); the clause (إن الله) gives the reason for the preceding prohibition; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يحب المفسدين) is its khabar. (قالَ: إِنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ عِنْدِي): a resumption set out to answer their saying that what you have is a favour and blessing from Allah, so spend of it in thanks to Him who blessed you with it. (إنما) is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أوتيته) is a passive past verb; the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the hāʾ is the second direct object; (على علم) is in the position of a ḥāl from the deputy agent in (أوتيته); (عندي) is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of (علم), i.e. "I was only given it while I was characterised by the knowledge that I have". They said: there was among the Children of Israel none more learned in the Torah than he, after Moses and Aaron. (أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ قُوَّةً وَأَكْثَرُ جَمْعاً): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and the wāw is conjoined to something implied on which the hamza has entered, i.e. "did he know what he claimed, and did he not know…"; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; (يعلم) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم), its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Qārūn; (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (يعلم); (أن) and its noun, and the clause (قد أهلك) is its khabar; the agent of (أهلك) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah; (من قبله) are attached to (أهلك); (من القرون) is a ḥāl from «من هو أشد», put before it; (من) is a relative noun, the direct object of (أهلك); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أشد) the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative; (قوة) is a tamyīz (specification); (منه) are attached to (أشد); and (أكثر جمعا) is conjoined to (أشد منه قوة).
(وَلا يُسْئَلُ عَنْ ذُنُوبِهِمُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, linking the clause to what precedes by way of threat and warning, i.e. Allah is aware of the sins of the criminals and needs no asking about them. (لا) is negating; (يسأل) is a passive imperfect verb; (عن ذنوبهم) are attached to (يسأل); and (المجرمون) is the deputy agent.
(فَخَرَجَ عَلى قَوْمِهِ فِي زِينَتِهِ): the fāʾ is conjoined to (قال «إنما أوتيته على علم»), and what is between them is parenthetical; (على قومه) are attached to (خرج); (في زينته) are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "strutting in his adornment, moving about in his marvels". A lengthy description of the adornment in which he came out bedecked will come. (قالَ الَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا يا لَيْتَ لَنا مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ قارُونُ إِنَّهُ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ): the clause is resumptive, set out to describe the feeling that stirred believers and unbelievers alike when they saw this overflowing luxury and marvellous splendour, following the way of human beings in wishing for comforts. (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (يريدون) is the ṣila; (الحياة) is the direct object and (الدنيا) an adjective of (الحياة); (يا) is a vocative particle and the one addressed is omitted; (ليت) is a particle of wishing and accusative; (لنا) is its khabar and (مثل) its noun put after; (ما) is a relative noun, the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (أوتي) is the ṣila, and it is a passive past verb; and (قارون) is the deputy agent. This wishing is by way of ghibṭa, which is that a person wishes for the like of his fellow's blessing without wishing that it cease from him; whereas envy (ḥasad) is wishing for the blessing that the envied person enjoys and for its ceasing from him. In the ḥadīth:
"It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Does ghabṭ harm? He said: No, except as khabaṭ harms the ʿiḍāh." ʿIḍāh is every tree that grows large [Translator's note: the text has «يغطلم», evidently for «يعظم»] and has thorns, and khabaṭ is striking a tree with a stick so that its leaves fall. (إن) and its noun; the shifted lām; (ذو حظ) is its khabar; and (عظيم) is an adjective of (حظ). Ḥaẓẓ is luck and fortune (bakht, jadd); one says a man is mabkhūt and majdūd, just as one says so-and-so is dhū ḥaẓẓ, ḥaẓīẓ and maḥẓūẓ; and this world is nothing but allotted fortunes and lots.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ وَيْلَكُمْ): (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (أوتوا العلم) is the ṣila; and (ويلكم) is the object of an omitted verb, by way of deterrence, i.e. "may Allah bind your woe upon you". (ثَوابُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِمَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً وَلا يُلَقَّاها إِلَّا الصَّابِرُونَ): (ثواب الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير) the khabar; (لمن) are attached to (خير); the clause (آمن) is the ṣila; (عمل صالحا) is conjoined to (آمن); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (يلقاها) is a passive imperfect verb and the hāʾ is the second direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (الصابرون) is the deputy agent put after, and it is the first object. The pronoun refers to the rewarding or to righteous deeds. (فَخَسَفْنا بِهِ وَبِدارِهِ الْأَرْضَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you wish to know his fate and what his affair came to". (خسفنا) is a verb and its agent; (به) are attached to (خسفنا); (بداره) is conjoined to (به); and (الأرض) is the direct object. Khasf has many meanings, among them: khasafa al-makān, yakhsifu, khusūfan, of the pattern of ḍaraba, i.e. it went down into the earth and sank; khasafa al-qamar: its light went; khasafat al-ʿayn: its light went and it sank in; khasafa fī al-arḍ and khusifa bihi fīhā: he disappeared into it. In the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayra, with a weak chain, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever puts on a new garment and struts in it is swallowed into the earth from the brink of Hell, and he goes on sinking (yatajaljalu) in it, never reaching its bottom." In Fatḥ al-Bārī it says: "What the ḥadīth entails is that the earth does not consume his body, so one could make a riddle of it and say to us: An unbeliever whose body does not decay after death — and it is Qārūn." In the Qāmūs: tajaljul is sinking into the earth, moving and being shaken, and jaljala is moving [a thing].
(فَما كانَ لَهُ مِنْ فِئَةٍ يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَما كانَ مِنَ المُنْتَصِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (كان) is a past incomplete verb; (له) is its khabar put first; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (فئة) is genitive in form by (من) and nominative in position as the noun of (كان); the clause (ينصرونه) is an adjective of (فئة), or it is the khabar of (كان), with (له) attached to an omitted ḥāl. It is also permissible for (كان) to be complete (tāmma), with (فئة) the agent of (كان); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl from (فئة). (ما) is negating; (كان) is a past incomplete verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "he", referring to Qārūn; and (من المنتصرين) is the khabar of (كان). (وَأَصْبَحَ الَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْا مَكانَهُ بِالْأَمْسِ يَقُولُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أصبح) is a past incomplete verb; (الذين) is its noun; the clause (تمنوا) is the ṣila; (مكانه) is the direct object; (بالأمس) are attached to (تمنوا); and the clause (يقولون) is the khabar of (أصبح). It is also permissible for (أصبح) to be complete, with (الذين) the agent and the clause (يقولون) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying". (وَيْكَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ): concerning (وي) there are several schools; we choose one of them and will present the rest in the section on benefits. It is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I marvel"; the kāf is a preposition; (أن) is a particle resembling the verb, and it with what falls within its scope is in the position of genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (وي). The sense of the kāf here is causation, not likening. (الله) is its noun; the clause (يبسط الرزق) is the khabar of (أن); (الرزق) is the direct object; (لمن) are attached to (يبسط); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; (من عباده) is a ḥāl; and (يقدر) is conjoined to (يبسط). (لَوْلا أَنْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا لَخَسَفَ بِنا): (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence containing the sense of condition; (أن) and what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is necessarily omitted; (منّ الله) is a verb and its agent; (علينا) are attached to (منّ); the lām occurs in the answer of (لولا); the clause (خسف بنا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; and the object of (خسف) is omitted, i.e. "the earth". (وَيْكَأَنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الْكافِرُونَ): its i'rab has preceded, and more of it will come shortly; it is an emphasis (tawkīd) of what precedes it.

* Rhetoric:
1- Inversion (al-qalb):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَآتَيْناهُ مِنَ الْكُنُوزِ ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ» there is, in this expression, the figure of qalb, which has been discussed before. The original is "that the band would be weighed down with the keys", i.e. would rise with them with effort. Abū ʿUbayd said: It is like their saying "I presented the she-camel to the trough", whose original is "I presented the trough to the she-camel", and like the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
كأن سبيئة من بيت رأس ... يكون مزاجها عسل وماء
(As though a purchased wine from Bayt Raʾs, whose mixing is honey and water,)
على أنيابها أو طعم غضّ ... من التفاح هصره اجتناء
(were upon her teeth, or the taste of a fresh apple whose branch the plucking bent down.)
It is also narrated "كأن سلافة"; sulāfa is the first that flows from the juice of grapes. As for sabīʾa, it means "purchased": one says sabaʾa al-khamr, like naṣara, when he bought it. It is also narrated khabīʾa, i.e. kept in the jar (khābiya). Bayt Raʾs is a village in Syria famous for the quality of its wine. A disagreement occurred between the author of the Qāmūs and the author of al-Ṣiḥāḥ over sabīʾa: the author of the Qāmūs said that al-Jawharī erred, and that sabā al-khamr, sabyan and sibāʾan, means he carried it from one land to another. (مزاجها) is the khabar of (يكون) although it is definite, and (عسل) its noun although it is indefinite, whereas the rule was the reverse; so the speech has been inverted. Al-Fārisī interpreted it as (مزاجها) being accusative as a figurative adverb. It is also narrated with the three words in the nominative, the noun of kāna being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause (يكون) an adjective of (سبيئة).
